In this game you must "control" a nimble AC racing car that is busy on a path full of other computer-controlled vehicles looking for a head-on collision to destroy your car. It is useless to underline the need to have excellent reflexes as the opponents' movements are very fast and sudden and will even feint at your vehicle to throw you off. So your work is to try to get to the finish line unharmed, for at most you can collide with 3 other cars. Bonus items will appear to help you from time to time. They can give you more points or special abilities such as greater speed, or a higher jump. 

Published in Italy as Azione Radiocomandata in Game 2000 Nuova serie n.19 (luglio/agosto 1989) and as Azione Radioc in Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - commodore plus (1989).

175490.overview: Al Barakah is a 2003 SEUCK game developed by Mariano Palao for the 2003 SEUCK Game Compo. It is a vertically scrolling shooter where many of the ships will take more than a single shot to destroy. Boss fights require you to take out the big ship in sections. As you progress through levels you will find the enemies shoot far more erratically so it is harder to avoid their shots.

175601.overview:
The year 2990 has come. The X time taken. Everything seemed to go smoothly in the small town of Barninghum where almost all the industrious inhabitants are employed in the nearby nuclear station. But suddenly a technician notices that the safe alarm systems indicate an overheating of the cooling system. Something has gone wrong! The evacuation plan is immediately implemented. Once everyone is out, the security system bars the doors, but at this point Dr. Jennings realizes that his secretary has not gone out with everyone else. After a quick review it is established with certainty that she must be locked inside the dangerous building. You must find the necessary keys that will be used to open the various doors of the office complex and then air vehicles to reach the area where the girl must be hidden. Or work to reach the reactor room and restore the upset order. 

Published in Italy as Android Chase in both Hit Parade C64 n.18 (Dicembre 1987) and in I Magnifici 5 & 7 n.24 (maggio 1987).

175649.overview: A text adventure with the simplest title, from the Melbourne House book "The Computer & Video Games - Book of Adventure". You will need to map the desert as you go if you want to get to the good stuff.

175681.overview: For two players, sail around the course and beat the yanks. Released as part of the 2-Up game pack.

175749.overview:
A two pack of text adventure mysteries, written in Adventurewriter/Quill including  "The Mystery of the Clock Seller" & "The Adventure of the Rosetta Stone".

The Mystery of the Clock Seller: The game finds Holmes and Watson trying to unravel the events that led to the death of Otto Meinwold - seller of fine antique clocks. Scotland Yard thinks the case is rather clear-cut. That Meinwold, found strangled with a pendulum cord from a Grandfather clock, was murdered for the daily take from his shop. Holmes believes there is much more to it.

The Adventure of the Rosetta Stone: Holmes is up against the mysterious "French Reclamation League" and their threat to steal this famous artifact.

176382.overview:
A text adventure game published as a type-in game in the book "Castles & Kingdoms".

A cold desert wind whipped across the dunes. Iron Knife stirred under the coarse blanket, opened one eye just a little, then closed it again, determined to wring the last moment of sleep from the night. As the light of the dawn grew brighter, the burdenbeast began to stir. The wind began to fade and the last wisps of smoke from the dying camp-fire hung over the camp like a shroud. Iron Knife was awake, though his eyes were still closed. He thought about the legend that had brought him into this miserable outback, a story spun by the most gifted and respected of all  the minstrels of Graylockland. It had been Freerover the Bard who'd been story-telling in that Belestrian market-place; his tale was that of a Wizard in recluse, a necromantic power so awesome that no one dare seek him out as long as he breathed. But now he breathed no longer, according to the bard, and only stories guarded his treasure - and a spider called Shadow. Wealth heyond imagination, beyond dreaming, lay inside that mountain. Iron Knife opened his eyes to the day. He rose quickly, stashed the carry sacks he'd been using as a pillow, and slung them aboard the hurdenbeast. "No dawdling today, you ill-tempered, foul-breathed creature, II he thought, "for today is the day Iron Knife makes his mark on the world." Beyond the edge of the outback, rising like a needle in the eye of the Gods, Spider Mountain protruded into the dawn sky. It stood, foreboding, yet beckoning, but whether it offered treasure or death, who could say? Off in the distance, almost at the base of the mountain, lay a village. At an angle to the village, there was a hint of a road. Iron Knife chose the village. As he came into town, the shimmering desert heat had become overpowering. He trudged through the abandoned ruins, his eye catching a sign on an intact building. 'Tavern', it said, and seemed to invite him in. Dusty, musty and smelling of time and neglect, it still felt good compared to the heat outside. Iron Knife allowed his eyes to play over the ruined interior: broken glass,  shattered chairs, and on the only upright table there lay an unused torch. "What luck," he exclaimed, "a bottle of Ambrosia!" He moved over to the shelf where the Ambrosia sat so invitingly. Caressing it appreciatively, he popped the cork and quaffed the contents in one mighty gulp. The room began to spin around, and he crashed to the floor. He slept for a full day and night, and woke with a throbbing head that felt as if all the Royal Guardsmen were tramping through it. While his head cleared, he looked around. A box of assorted quarrels and darts lay in disarray on the floor; he had knocked them over as he fell. A lever had been pulled downwards, although he did not remember doing it. Beyond that, a trapdoor in the floor yawned open. "The treasure of Spider Mountain," cried Iron Knife aloud, "lies beyond that doorway.

177133.overview:
Atic Atac is a 2020 homebrew C64 conversion of the ZX Spectrum classic of the same name. This game was developed by Tomaz "Tom-Cat" Kac with music by Saul Cross, and graphics by Steve Day.

Game description: 


As the game begins, the player character falls through a trapdoor and ends up inside an evil castle with only one way to get out of it - find all the pieces of the great ACG key that unlocks the main door.

Atic Atac is an action game with adventure elements, mixing arcade gameplay with exploration of a large castle and light puzzle-solving. The player can choose to control either a Wizard, a Knight, or a Serf. Each character has access to a different secret passage, which means that the player will be navigating different rooms depending on the choice of character. Characters also possess unique skills: for example, the Serf can gain momentum when running, allowing him to traverse greater distances in less time.

Enemies appear in each room and would randomly attack the protagonist. The player can choose to collide with them, which destroys the enemies but also drains health from the main character. Some enemies cannot be killed by conventional means and must be either avoided or dealt with by using special items. Poisonous mushrooms will also damage the hero, and bosses will drain his health as long as he maintains close contact.

The player character's life meter gets gradually depleted. Health can be restored by consuming food scattered around the castle, but the countdown cannot be stopped. In addition, doors would sometimes close, trapping the hero in a room. Keys must be collected to open many of the castle's doors.

177711.overview:
A pong\airhockey type competition game where you make points by smashing the ball into the goal of your opponent. The call can be deviated by different objects in the field. The fire button will increase your speed but you have limited energy to strike a balance. Defend your goal while various beings wander around the screen, they can be destroyed in a hit but will unpredictably deflect the ball. A colored square may appear and hitting it can add some special effects such as immobilizing the opponent, allowing you to catch the ball, increase speed or reversing your controls!

Published as Affronto in Italy in Tutto C64 n.5 (1992/1993) and in Formula 64 n.106.

178394.overview:
The heroes of the most famous videogames, after completing their missions, joined forces, founded the h.r.g. (hero rebel group) and have conquered the coin-op world.

 Among the main exponents of the group are: Commando, Vaus, Goblins, Bub & Bob, Tiger Shark, Mario, Jack, Rygar, Pac-Man.

Their leader and current coin-op emperor is unknown. You, in the role of Ryu, a renegade of H.R.G., moved away after learning of their evil plans, and have decided to fight them

 You are alone, armed with your ax and your shield and... with your courage. To free the coin-op world you must first vanquish the enemy hordes present on its 4 natural satellites governed in order by: Commando, Vaus, Goblins and Bub & Bob, then launch the decisive attack on the planet in search of the emperor.

On your way you will find, in addition to enemies, objects and people to be brought to safety. for example: prisoners, capsules, armor, crowns and joysticks that have been lost by your enemies. Once you reach the emperor, it is your job to try and kill him. 

Good luck, you will need it !!!

Created using the Shoot 'em up Construction Kit.

178582.overview:
The computer games collection Arcade Force Four was released in 1988 and was marketed by the company U.S. Gold. It contains the four games:

Road Runner (Action)
Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom (Action)
Metrocross (Motorcross simulation)
Gauntlet and the Deeper Dungeons (Action shooter).

178601.overview: Published in the Italian Commodore games magazine: Hit Parade 64 N°14 (07-08/1987) but originally released the year prior. This tenth set of Boulder Dash maps was released by Don Pedro originally.

178641.overview:
You are trapped in the space base of the enemy planet Vectron, defended by sophisticated armaments. To escape you must be able to cross with your astro-fighter various sectors equipped with missiles and laser cannons and patrolled by fierce squadrons of spaceships. Your spacecraft and armed with air-to-air missiles; so do not hesitate to launch yourself into this moral combat where weapons cannot replace reflexes, courage and determination. Remember that the only way to escape is barred by a wall: take it down before crashing into it and get ready to glaze piece by piece the mighty mother ship while avoiding enemy fire in the meantime. Full speed ahead!

Published in Digital Marketing PD #021 as Kill 'em All. 

Published in Published in Hit Parade 64 N°63 (01/1992) as Avanti Tutta.

179228.overview: Released by the Belgium/German scene group Raiders of the Lost Empire (R.O.LE.), this sequel to the 1990 Spectrum text adventure game was created for the 64 by Larry aka John Wilson Zenobi and in this one you return to Oblivion where you must explore the ship, repair it, and return to Earth to collect your bonus. But first, survive.

179251.overview: Released as part of the SEUCK Compo 2019. As a spider thief runner, grab treasure from the lair of the mad spider queen and escape with your lode. Make your way through an insane labyrinth of terrors including such dastardly denizens as spiders (of course), giant deadly dragonflies, woeful webs of bondage and flesh-eating flies!

179261.overview:
Arcade Hall of Fame is a compilation containing the following five games:

Spy Hunter
Tapper
Up ‘N’ Down
Blue Max
Aztec Challenge

179382.overview: A break out style game totally written in (compiled) basic by Francesco Clementoni (known as Arturo Dente on the demoscene) . It features some interesting ideas like sub-games in the game play and a nice little animated story before the playing stages.

179396.overview:
Alone is a puzzle/brain game which both the year of release and game's developer are currently unknown. 

Description:

Someone has disturbed the arrangement of the letter-table (alphabet). It is your task to reorganize the letters to the original arrangement (where it has been before)

180087.overview:
A stimulating super Space Shuttle shooter. The game seems heavily influenced by the arcade classic, Astro Blaster. The Omega 4 Square Sphere space ship, built with new and exotic scientific techniques, was destined for the exploration of the newly discovered Zone 8, being particularly feared due to the alien forces that populate it. But an unexpected threat is headed for the eastern United States and the ship is the only one that can intervene in time! Waves of meteorites that intend to rain down on the earth and create an extinction event. Destroy all the meteorites, you are the only hope for the world. 

Published in Italy as New York Attack, shortened to Attak in Poke n.13 (maggio 1986).

180200.overview:
An OUTSTANDING ultra-fast machine language game!  15 frantic levels of difficulty!  Alien saucers swoop and dive in a relentless attack!  Fear not!  You have an awesome wonder weapon:  you unleash a bolt of incredible power from your laser/heat ray/particle beam/thermonuclear cannon, which atomizes these marauding good-for-nothin' saucers!  C64 arcade action.

Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/02 (Issue #08), COMPUTE!'s Second Book of C64 Games, Happy Computer 1987/11 and re-released in the 75 Spill Data-Tronic compilation.

It was also released by Italian publisher Mantra Software in MC 1009 under the names Astro Panico, and also Astropanico in 1984 as well.

180201.overview:
You have been volunteered to save the city of Pawtucket from certain attack by the evil inhabitants of the Isle of Sportta Sappa and their only ICBM with a nuclear warhead. Destroy the missile without sacrificing yourself. 

You've been dropped off on an island about a mile west of Sportta Sappa. you've been given some petty cash in the amount of $150. Peering to the north and west you see nothing but trees. To the east is some seaweed, the shore line and beyond that, the island of Sportta Sappa. To the south is a steep trail leading up a cliff about a hundred feet high. The next move is yours!

180294.overview:
Air Combat is a two player vs only shooter game in which one player controls a black airplane, and the other player controls a blue airplane. The goal of the game is to take out your opponent until he /she is completely out of lives.

This game was developed by Antti Kylonen and Juha Ervasi and published by Protcol Productions Oy in the Finnish based disk magazine Floppy Magazine 64. Issue: 1998/1.

180295.overview: Pac-Man clone with some twists. You're a space bear Astex and you try to collect points while avoiding multiple type of enemies: some of them follow you Pac-Man style while others are territorial.  Extra walls appear from time to time. The game is over when you either lose all the bears all the timer runs out. Published in MikroBitti Magazine 1986.

180471.overview:
Auto 64 is a racing themed avoid-it style game by David Swinnterton published as a type-in listing in the Your Computer 1985/06 magazine. 

The goal is not to win the race, but to not crash into the other cars for as long as you can.

180503.overview: AL II is a vertically scrolling 2D shoot'em up, originally published in a French computer magazine Hebdogiciel N°117 (10.01.1986). The planet AL 2 has decided to invade the earth. For this, she installed missiles on the far side of the moon. On board your ship you must destroy the missile launch pads. To destroy them you have to aim for the opening at the top of the silos. It's up to you to find the right height. Be careful because the fuel of the ship is limited.

180634.overview: Äänimuistipeli is a Finnish language 2 player only memory game. However, instead of flipping tiles (or in this case diamonds) when you click a diamond it plays a sound, then you have to match that diamond with another diamond that makes the same sound.

180658.overview: A sex quiz, geared for females.

180888.overview:
Educational game developed by Chris Raiskums and Robert Lee. It was published by Commodore Educational Software in 1983.

This game questions the player on the geometrical measurements of Azimuth and Altitude.

180895.overview: An action pinball game released on PCS Club Disk #22. Created with The Pinball Construction Set by Charles M Duncan.

180896.overview:
Awalé, though little known in Europe, is one of the world's most widely played games. It is played throughout Africa and can be found under a variety of names and with different formats. This version comes from a region of the Ivory Coast, called Baoule, and is a game for two players.

The equipment is very simple: a board, generally made of wood, which has had hollows carved in it, (most usually there are 12 for the game itself and often another 2 to hold the players' gains), and 48 grains, so-called because in the original these would have been whatever was to hand - perhaps coffee beans or pebbles.

Each row of 6 hollows represents the camp of one of the players, known as north and south. At the start of the game, each position holds 4 grains. The 2 positions for the players' gains are empty. North (or the computer) plays first. The game is played by distributing the contents of one of the player's own positions around the board in an
ant-clockwise direction.

Each player in turn takes all the contents from the chosen position and distributes them one at a time until none is left, missing the starting point if going round more than once.
The last position added to is checked to see if it is both in the opponent's camp and now contains either 2 or 3 grains. If so, the player takes all the grains from that position and adds them to their own gains, in the place designated for these, then moves back one position to apply the same 2 tests. This continues until a square is not in the opponent's camp or does not hold 2 or 3 grains (or both).

A player can defend a position from attack by moving the threatened grains, by taking the threatening grains or by moving grains in such a way as to make the intended attack pointless or impossible.

If one player has no grains left in their camp, the other must 'feed' them by making a move which will place grains in the opponent's camp, if such a move is possible, thus allowing the game to continue.

The winner is the first player to amass 25 or more grains. In the event of a stalemate, the game can be abandoned (by pressing C= Q) and the winner is the player with the most gains. Choose your position by pressing its letter key, change your mind as many times as you like, then press RETURN to make your move.

180954.overview:
In 1986, Tapanimäki completed a text adventure game (in Finnish) inspired by Infocom's games called Aikaetsivä (Time Detective in English), for which Tampere-based Triosoft reserved publishing rights.

The game was briefly mentioned in MikroBitti magazine in the “Commodore insider” column and was advertised with the slogan “buy a Finnish game!”. However, the game was never released because the publisher did not consider the potential economic benefits to be covered even to cover marketing costs.

In the amateur circles of Finnish text games and science fiction, Time Detective was well received, and it was even compared to a novel made into a game.

181404.overview: Archer is a side scrolling game in which your goal is the diffuse a bomb. It was developed using Garry Kitchen's GameMaker. This is not to be confused with the sample game of the same name which came built into GameMaker itself.

181901.overview:
This version has only 2 of the 4 levels from the arcade game has simplistic graphics and came on cartridge and tape. In version 2 of the game was reissued on disk. The disk version has contemporary graphics and all four levels of the arcade game (Level 1 (v.1) = Level 1 (v.2), Level 2 (v.1) = Level 4 (v.2). The game principle of the two comparable levels has approx. stayed the same.

In Congo Bongo you take over the role of a jungle hunter who tries to catch a Gorilla named "Congo Bongo". In each of the two levels there are numerous perils between you and Congo in the shape of abysses, torrential rivers, falling coconuts, monkeys gone wild, snakes and rhinos. But hippos, huge piranhas and floating lily leaves will help in crossing the rivers and also monkeys that have taken a seat on your back can be shaken off again . . .

182236.overview: Created in 2002 by Zoltán Scserbin. The exact same game with different graphics comes under the names Dig Dug Dash 01, Invasion Dash 01, Robot Dash 01 and Auto Dash 01, but is best known by the 2003 naming Golden Boulder - Who Dares Wins 01!

182460.overview: A music+visual title. Guide your little white square around the screen, and avoid crashing into obstacles which appear. In some parts of the game, you'll need to get yourself into a very tight position. This game is cleverly constructed in order to test your memory, from where you lose last time. Try to score as many points as you possibly can (or reach 999 points.

182506.overview:
Alchimia is a strange little Italian language shooter in which you play an exterminator in a science lab shooting down flies.

It was developed bY Enrico Meloni and published by CESE s.r.l. in Amico Bit #3

182522.overview: Published as a game of the "Cassette 50" collection / Digital Marketing PD #234 / a.k.a. "Avoid Water" You must avoid falling through the gaps in the bridges by forming an ice bridge across the gaps. Points gained by distance traveled without falling

182876.overview: After 7 years Arno is back with a new BD release. As usual this game has 16 caves and 4 intermissions in varying difficulty, all classic style, and with open borders in several caves.

182928.overview: Shooter created by Dr. ICE of IRS using the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit, and featuring 2 player cooperative play.

183305.overview: A SEUCK-based shooter with an underwater twist. Published in Commodore Disk User 1988/05-06. Atlantis: the fabled and feared lost continent. At last, the quest of a lifetime is finished and our are free to explore the cycolopean ruins of lost cities at your leisure. Except that life isn't that simple. Atlantis teems with cybernated creatures of all sorts and it'll take all your expertise and the power of your mini-sub to win through to the final secret.

183790.overview: The unreleased Armalyte 2 on the C64. It is pretty much just a sprite swap of the main ship as the level itself is from the original Armalyte. The sequel was to have been programmed by the immaculate Cyberdyne Systems, a few ideas were placed. The main ship was to be more colourful, the aliens more intelligent and a power-up shop was to be included too. It was to borrow more from Salamander too! The game was to feature around 6 levels in total, and just the one player to fit in all the improvements. Flickering problems from the first game were to be removed and other various improvements. Unfortunatly, Cyberdyne Systems were contracted out to System 3, and after getting to work on projects for System 3, such as Deadlock and Last Ninja 3. Armalyte 2 was shelved.

185505.overview: Interesting adventure with moving main character. Escape from where they have you locked up, get what you need from the Saloon and prep to search for the outlaw in the desert, so keep your canteen filled. And when you find the outlaw, make sure your aim is true. Good luck pardner.

186448.overview:
Athanor - Awakening is the first in a trilogy. Its only ambition is to offer an adventure that you could have played 30 years ago!
In this first part, you play as a Franciscan monk in early 12th century Italy.
A lost abbey seems agitated by suspicious events.
Your order sends you to investigate and understand what is disturbing the monks.

Is this investigation the real motivation to take you on this journey?
You'll find out, but no matter what, fear not, your journey will surely take you further than you ever imagined.

"Do you have a whole night? "  If so, insert your floppy disk and browse through the first places.  You will not switch off until the early morning hours after having experienced hours of intense fever.

Source: http://www.safargames.fr/index.php/le-background

188531.overview: Apple Hunt is a simple collect 'em up game in which your character goes around collecting apples. It was developed by James Arlet and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/04 (Issue #22)

189204.overview: Air Attack is a crosshair shooter coded in BASIC. It is keyboard controlled only. The objective is to stop bombs before they hit the bottom of the screen. The game was developed by Kevin Bergin and published as a type-in by Duckworth Home Computing in Bergin's book "Commodore 64 Games".

189205.overview: Alien Kill is a vertically scrolling shooter in which the player's objective is to kill as many aliens as he/she can. The game has the option for two-player co-op play. It was developed by David Farrar using Chris Yates' SEUCK engine in 1988. Published in ECP's "Gold Ribbon Game Pak".

189206.overview: Alien Kill II: The Final Encounter is the sequel to the original game. This game like it's predecessor,  is a vertically scrolling shooter developed by Dave Farrar using Chris Yates' SEUCK engine. Also like it's predecessor, it too has the option for two-plyaer co-op play. This was was released the same year as the original game, 1988. Published in ECP's "Gold Ribbon Game Pak".

192118.overview:
The 1984 Atarisoft collection for the Commodore 64 was created by Bandit Breaking Service and includes all the AtariSoft games for the C64 with the exception of Battlezone and Galaxian, and the unreleased/leaked versions of Mario Brothers and Joust. Games included:

◉ Centipede
◉ Defender
◉ Dig Dug
◉ Donkey Kong
◉ Jungle Hunt
◉ Moon Patrol
◉ Ms. Pacman
◉ Pac-Man
◉ Pole Position
◉ Robotron: 2084

192161.overview:
Adventure is a clone/unofficial conversion of the Atari 2600 classic Adventure/RPG of the same name. This was developed by Donnie Russell II and released into the public domain. The year of release is not known.

A graphic dungeon quest inspired by the old mainframe game of the same name, Adventure is a graphic action-adventure game where you use your joystick to wander around, collecting keys to explore castles, labyrinths and everything in between, whilst slaying anything that moves (i.e. Dragons & Co.) to get treasures.

The game has 3 difficulty settings:

- Level 1 (Easiest)
- Level 2: The Kingdom is larger than Level 1, containing secret rooms and hidden items to add difficulty.
- Level 3 (Hardest): Similar to Level 2 but all objects/items are placed randomly throughout the Kingdom.

Gameplay revolves around picking up (and dropping) items, hacking your way though dragons, finding keys to open the castle gates and using magic (i.e. reincarnation) in case you get swallowed by failing-to-follow-their-diet-plan-dragons.

Groups +

192162.overview:
Swedish language text adventure developed by Peter Karlsson and published in the following:

- SYS PD Club64 #2 (1990)

- SYS PD Diskett#05 (1991)

- SYS PD Diskett#21 (1991)

192271.overview:
A puzzle game created by Tim Hartnell & Brett Hale and published in 1984 in the book "The Big Fat Book of Commodore 64 Games". This is a two-part game. The first part is very simple, but the speed with which you solve the easy problem (to work out which letter of the alphabet the computer is
thinking of) dictates how many moves you'll have to work out the solution to the second part. The second is a game somewhat like Invicta's Mastermind, except that instead of you having to guess a code of colors, the code here is made up from the first six letters of the alphabet.
The code could be ABeD, FDEA or even FFFF, or any other of the enormous number of possible combinations of those six letters. 
 
After-you've entered your guess, the computer will rate your answer. A plus sign (+) is awarded for each Letter which occurs in your code and in the computer's code, but not in the right position. So if the computer was thinking of ABCA and you entered CEEF, you would be awarded on a + sign. A correct Letter in the correct position gains you an asterisk (*). So, if you had entered AEEF when the computer was thinking of ABCA, you would be awarded an * as a result.

192413.overview:
The story takes place 50 BC. All of Gaul is occupied by the Romans ... all of Gaul? Never. A small village on the Kveste offers resistance. It is guarded by 4 roman camps. You now have to attack the small group. Good luck to you!

Published in Go Games n.7 (March 1986) as Fast Man.

192428.overview:
Piloting a landing module, you must disengage from the support spaceship and attempt a soft landing on the planet Zombi. The module is equipped with small thrusters that you will need to use to mitigate the descent and to land safely on the ramp that will appear on the screen. Instrumentation on-board will report all the parameter which you will need to take into account. 

Published in Italy as Pilota Astrale in Go Games n.10 (Giugno 1986) and in Super Game 2000 N°10 (Dicembre 1985) as Recupera i Cristalli.

192671.overview:
Akalabeth: World of Doom is a an unofficial homebrew conversion of  the Apple II classic of the same name for the Commodore 64.

This game was developed in 2016 by Dungeoneer Games & Simulations (DGS), which was a trio consisting of Antonello Morella, Andrea Schincaglia, and Dávid Vigh (Grass).

Game Description:

Once, the land of Akalabeth was peaceful and quiet. But then came Mondain, an evil and ambitious man who created dungeons and populated them with foul creatures. The noble warrior British was able to drive Mondain from Akalabeth, but the monsters he brought with him remain.

As either a fighter or a mage, it is your job to explore Akalabeth, descend into the dungeons and vanquish the beasts dwelling within. On an overhead map of the land, one can find the dungeons, towns where one may buy supplies, weapons and armor, and a castle, where one will be given quests by Lord British. To fulfill such a quest, a certain type of creature must be destroyed in a dungeon.

Inside the dungeons, the view switches to a first-person perspective. Fight, explore and find treasure on your way to complete a quest. Each successive quest will require you to destroy a stronger monster, which will reside on a deeper dungeon level than the one before it.

193667.overview: Army Leader is a single-player war strategy game developed by Geir H. Hansen and published by Gameblaster in 1988. The game is in Norwegian,

194925.overview: A 2 Player only dueling game of "The Big 100" collection, part of the "Star Fighter" game pack. Published as Astronaut Battle in Compute mit 1986/01.

195142.overview: Aksjemarked (translates to Stock Market) is a Norwegian language turn based (up to six players) stock market simulation for the Commodore 64. It was published by Datavarehuset in 1982.

195514.overview:
Artillery is an adaptation of the well known formula. Players take turn firing their artillery shots at the enemy. They only have to provide an angle and amount of gunpowder (for distance). The wind changes strength and direction each turn which has to be taken into calculation. The levels are randomly generated between every game and shells that are fired leave a small crater. If a player hits the other player the game is over. This version features only two player hot-seat play.

Originally released for Commodore PET in 1979, the game was later released for C64 on multiple computer magazines as a type-in program in early 80s. Released as part of the 20 program Canadian only compilation called Commodore 64 Program Pack.

195529.overview: An airplane flies across the screen above a city with skyscrapers. When the plane reaches the far end of the screen, it reappears on the other end, but at a lower altitude since it is running out of fuel. The objective is to drop bombs on the city to destroy all buildings so that the plane may land on level ground.

195671.overview: A SEUCK shooter created by Dr. Ice of IRS. featuring 2 player simultaneous, cooperative play. The Xenians are a people who represent a constant danger to the interstellar Federation. In fact, they continue to make border rids, attacking numerous convoys. The Federation has, of course, tried several times to attack the Xenian post but unfortunately always without success. They are perched inside the planet Xenia, whose entrance consists of a very narrow and also very well defended tunnel. Many pilots have already given up their lives and therefor the Federation has decided to suspend any further attacks. This does not mean that he will remain and watch: in fact he has developed a simulator on which to train the pilots and only hose who manage to pass this extremely difficult test will have th honor of attempting to defeat the Xenians!

195672.overview: Alien Commando: Planet Ice is the third and final game in the Alien Commando shooter trilogy, created with SEUCK by Dr. Ice of IRS and featuring 2 person simultaneous cooperative play.

195693.overview: Alien Raid is a Spanish language shoot'em up, where you defend the city from the alien ships, released in 1985 by Microjet/Stars Commodore.

195703.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter published in Commodore Disc #56. Survive a thousand dangers...

195704.overview: A Brain\Puzzle\Logic game for one or two players in vs mode by Thunders (with  Méhész Leventea doing code and graphics and SFX and music by Sándor Fodor, and released to the Public Domain in 1994.

195705.overview: A Brain\Logic board game for one or two players, created by Smart Works for Rom Software. Very much like an extended noughts and crosses or Tic-Tac-Toe game.

195749.overview:
A Swedish language text and graphics adventure game. Jaktkommando Arne Weise (probably "Hunting Commando Arne Weise") is an adventure game by Swedish programmer Johan Rosengren. The game uses a first person perspective with monochrome illustrations. The controls are menu-driven. You can choose between five commands (use, take, give, go and hit).
Arne Weise is the name of a Swedish journalist and TV host who was very famous in Sweden.

195750.overview: You might call this the prequel to the "Borodino: 1812 - Napoleon in Russia" game put out by Krentek Software the same year as this one, as this battle happened the day before that larger engagement.

195751.overview: Preceeded by "Assembloids" in 2012, this version was dropped for New Year in 2014 with someone noting that, "the most independently-ported game of 2010's gets another port", this time a BASIC one. This would be followed by an improved BASIC version in 2017 called Assembloids BASIC 2.0.

195752.overview: Funny oddball shooter where you have to guide your spaceship through an assortment of mazes, avoiding some very strange nasties along the way! Enjoyable!

196124.overview:
Ai confini della realtà means On the Edge of Reality and it is an Italian language text adventure created by Fabrizio Fornasiero  and published in Commodore 64 Club #02 [Italian Release]. You are in a plane whose engine has been struck by lightening. The plane loses altitude and you, a young and brilliant successful manager, decide to abandon the plane so you can save yourself. As the parachute opens you see the burning plane above you moving away into the low clouds and then nothing... 
 
A terrible gust of wind breaks one of the parachute straps and you fall heavily into the icy waters of the Atlantic Ocean; you feel your legs stiffen but you still manage to free yourself from the parachute; you lose consciousness. The sunbeam hits your eyes and you wake up on a sunny beach... deserted, it seems. After the first moment of confusion you decide to explore the island and try to understand where you might find yourself. You probably don't understand much about navigation and nautical maps but the presence of an island in the center of the Atlantic Ocean is quite suspicious and you wouldn't really be able to give it a name... at least not rationally.

However, it is useless to stay on the beach and wait; it is necessary instead to start exploring the island and look for some possibility of salvation....

196464.overview: Made with Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit (SEUCK), Al Capone can be described as drive-by shooter. You drive around on the countryside, shooting gangsters that are walking around the area.

197235.overview: The Acorn Court is a text adventure developed by Todd S. Murchison for the Commodore 64, and released into the public domain in 1997.

197236.overview:
Acorn Man in Magic Land is a vertical scrolling shooter in which you play the character of "Acorn Man" It was developed by Roberto Ricioppo using Chris Yates' SEUCK engine and released in 2012.

Adventures have always been fun, but not for poor Acorn Man. He's traveled to magic land to find that the villages and woods are not as nice as they used to be. An evil wizard cast a spell over the villagers, and turned them into various characters. Acorn Man comes to the rescue and he has to break spells on the creatures, simply by throwing acorns at them. Can Magic Land be restored to a good place how it used to be. Or will the evil wizard reign of Magic Land remain forever ?

197250.overview: Action Def is a game developed by Christian Siege using Chris Yates and Jonathan Wells Sideways SEUCK mod. It was released as part of the 2011 Sideways SEUCK competition.

197258.overview: The Battle of Austerlitz was one of the most important and decisive engagements of the Napoleonic Wars. In what is widely regarded as the greatest victory achieved by Napoleon, french forces defeated the larger Russian and Austrian armies and brought the war to a rapid end. The battle is often cited as a tactical masterpiece. Your goal is to repeat that masterpiece in this french strategy game designed for serious gamers.

197351.overview: A Story is a computerized version of the popular Mad Libs word game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Pat Tubbs, and released in 1983 as part of CBM Public Domain - English I.

197536.overview:
An "avoid it" style game in which you must survive by avoiding falling asteroids in your space ship for as long as you can. This was developed by Vanja J. Utne and released as part of a 2002 mini-game competition.

An updated shoot 'em up version called Astrostorm II was being developed in 2006, but never got past the preview/playable demo stage.

197850.overview: A basic side-scrolling shooter with some similarities to games like Scramble, but also has some resemblance to Defender as well. This was developed by Alan Bond and released as a public domain game in 1986.

197851.overview: Alien Battle II is the sequel to Alien Battle. Like the original, this was also a side-scrolling shooter developed by Alan Bond and released into the public domain in 1986 (the same year as the first game). However, unlike the original, this game has a few more original gameplay elements, and isn't basically a Scramble clone like the original game was.

197958.overview:
Al-Khwarizmi is a number based memory game for two players only that also has some resemblance to Ralph Baer's classic game SImon. The goal of the game is to push on the number keys as the computer selects them (There are only nine). The computer keeps adding numbers until you get one wrong, and then it goes to the second player. The player with the highest score at the end is the winner.

This game was developed by Robert Young and Paul Copeland and published in 1983 by Penguin Books as a type-in listing in their book "The Penguin Book of Commodore 64 Games"

198428.overview: Addition Tic Tac Toe is a math based Tic Tac Toe game that revolves around addition. It is a conversion of an old Commodore Plus/4 game. The conversion was done by Barry "Cout" Hart in 2017.

198681.overview: A French language 3D platformer, Q*bert's French brother, by Gilles Siffert and published in Hebdogiciel N°081 (03.05.1985). Albert is a game that consists of repainting all the bricks of a wall by simply jumping on them. Of course, we won't let you do as you please. So don't be surprised to see two pretty snakes rushing at you.

198682.overview:
After multiple adventures, you managed to enter the cave of ALI BABA, with the intention of bringing back some 'memories' ...

Unfortunately, the genie spots you and tries to lock you up by blocking the corridors with his magical fluid, which in seconds turns into the hardest stone, unless you destroy it beforehand.

You can come out of the cave only by taking all the treasure. You will then have to face a more powerful genie: indeed, its walls solidify more quickly.

Each time a new wall is built, your score decreases by 100 points. The goal of the game is to hold as long as possible, before the score is zero.

Published in Hebdogiciel N°027 (13.04.1984). 

40 bonus points per table
Additional dependent bonus
The time taken to take the last 20 to 30
ATTENTION: this last bonus can be negative.
   If you want to go to the next table without finishing, type _.
In this case, all will turn into walls ...
Pressing the spacebar, the game stops until you press a key."

198683.overview: A shoot'em-up created by Pascal Lin and published in Hebdogiciel N°026 (06.04.1984). You are in command of the starfighter. Your mission is to repel the invaders without getting hit by the bombs. For each ship repelled you get10 points.To continue, type on C. In this game you only live twice! At 50 points a surprise awaits you.

198684.overview: A French language puzzle game created by Claude Baisnee and published in Hebdogiciel N°083 (17.05.1985) and N°084 (24.05.1985). You have to get the yellow square out of the box by sliding the coins to clear the way. To do this, you will place the black dot on a piece with the joystick then by pressing the red button you orient the handle in the direction where you want to move the piece. If the movement is possible, it will take place, otherwise nothing will happen. Up to you!

198685.overview: A Skramble style shooter created by Cyril Cambien and published in Hebdogiciel N°035 (08.06.1984).

198853.overview: Another Bloody Adventure is a public domain suspense filled text adventure developed by John Broad. It was released on ICPUG Adventure Disc #1. The actual year of release is not currently known.

199171.overview: Attack of the Petscii Robots is a top-down action/puzzle game. It is inspired by oblique top-down projection games like Ultima, but takes much of the gameplay concepts from first-person shooters. The object is to destroy all of the robots. To do this, you have to search objects in the game for weapons and other items to help you along the way. Many scenarios require complex thinking and problem solving, rather than just action shooting.

199397.overview: Atom Heart is a strange vertical shooter developed by Mo Dernart for the 2018 SEUCK competition. Shoot the aliens and anything that shoots at you. Watch for open caves, which spawn bats.

199555.overview: Logitrumps is a card game, like we used to play it in the 80's similar to the card game "War". Each player (you and the computer) gets the same number of cards. Each card represents a retro computer and has several values like Year, memory, colors, RAM, etc. Each card has strength and weaknesses. If a computer has a lot of memory or colors, it usually isn't that old and therefor would likely lose in the year category. Usually the higher value wins with the exception of the year where the lower value wins. The player to win all the cards through strategic match-ups wins the game.

201123.overview: An Italian language, secret agent themed, text adventure, the second in a trilogy of games, with graphics created by Alessandro Zanello and published in Next Strategy n.09 (06/1986).

201126.overview: An Italian language, pirate themed text adventure with graphics. It was created by Alessandro Zanello. This was the second part of a trilogy published in Next Strategy (n.8 through Next Strategy n.10) preceded by Alberto Sorrio: La Goccia di Sangue and followed by Alberto Sorrio: L'Ereditiera.

201144.overview: Alan Simmons: Bucaneer is a pirate tehemed Italian language graphic text adventure. It was developed by Bonaventura Di Bello and published by Edizioni Hobby in Viking No.08 (09/1987).

201152.overview:
Your mission is to arrange the grid so that no alien is on the same row or column as another alien of the same color. How you accomplish this depends on which mode of play you have selection from the options menu. There are three modes of play...

1. Switch 'em:

Use the CRSR (cursor) keys (or the joystick in port 2) to move the white rectangle (all modes) on the alien you want to select and press return (enter). Now select another alien the same way. The two aliens will swap places on the grid

2. Slide 'em:

In this mode you slide rows or columns of aliens up, down, left, or right using the following keys:

•  space bar: slide aliens left
•  space bar+shift key: slide aliens right
•  return: slide aliens up
•  shift+return: slide aliens down

3. Rotate 'em:

In this mode, you will rotate groups of eight aliens left or right. Press space to rotate to the left, and press return to rotate to the right

This game was developed by Anthony "Fogweaver" Rose and published in Loadstar#157 in 1997.

203323.overview: A SEUCK based horizontal shooter created by Phillip Bayliss.

203346.overview: A crosshairs style shooter created using the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit by Philip Bayliss.

203347.overview: A vertically scrolling shooter created using the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit by a creator who goes by the name Dreamworks. No, not DreamWorks...just Dreamworks. This game allows for cooperative multi-play for two users. While there is competition for points, you can certainly go much farther with two players and many situations are much more difficult without a second person.

203373.overview: In this adventure you play as a lady courier that must deliver a package to the upper level floor, but what starts of as a routine job ends up going completely disastrous and it's down to you to escape and to find out what had happened.

203676.overview:
Adventure 14: Return to Pirate's Isle is an unofficial source code hack of the old Scott Adams' game of the same name. The original game was only released on the Texas Instruments TI-99/4A, but in late 2019 someone used a Z-Code website to convert the game to make it runnable on the C64.

This was the sequel to Pirate Cove/Pirate Adventure.

Desciption;

Created exclusively for the TI, Return to Pirate's Isle was the only Scott Adams adventure which did NOT require the TI Adventure cartridge, available separately. It is still subject to debate whether this is truly #14 in the series or whether it does not count since it was only made for the TI.

It uses the same parser and interface as the other games in the series, and challenges you to return to Pirate's Isle in search of treasure yet again.

You may want to speed up the emulation, as the game does run a bit slow compared to the original Texas Instruments version.

203712.overview:
Alhambra is a solitaire card game which is played using two decks of playing cards. Its unusual feature is akin to that of Crazy Quilt: the cards in the reserve are built either on the foundations or on a waste pile. 

Rules

There are 8 foundation piles. Four of these start with Aces and build up in suit, while the other four start with Kings and build down in suit. There are also 8 reserve piles containing four cards each. The top cards of the reserve piles are available only to be built on the foundation or onto the waste pile if they match the suit and are one rank higher or lower than the top card; there is no building on the reserve.

The deck deals out 1 card at a time, and if that card cannot be used, it will go to the waste pile, where it is available to be built onto the foundations.

When the stock is exhausted, the waste pile (which by then already includes cards from the reserve) is picked up and turned over to become the new stock. This can be done twice in the entire game.

The game finishes soon after the stock is exhausted the third time. The game is won when all cards are built into the foundation

The C64 version of the game was developed by Maurice Jones and published by J & F Publishing in their "8 More" compilation pack. The year that this game was made is however currently unknown.

205396.overview:
Developed in 2015 by Roberto Ricioppo using SEUCK, this shooter has no real story. The goal is simple, destroy the waves of alien baddies in every sector until 1. The game ends or 2. You lose all your lives.

Unlike a good portion of SEUCK games on TND, the music was not done by Richard Bayliss, rather Ricioppo did the music on this one himself.

205447.overview:
Word Master is a 1-player educational game for multiple systems.

A word appears in the center of the screen, and 8 surrounding words slowly fire towards the player. The player must rotate a turret to shoot the antonym of the word that appears in the middle of the screen. If the player shoots the correct block, a new word appears in the middle of the screen. The player must shoot all 8 words before the approaching gunfire reaches the center of the game field.

205492.overview:
The Authentic Tetris is an unofficial conversion of Atari's arcade conversion of the classic puzzle game. This conversion was developed by P.A.N.O.R.A.M.A. (on coding and music) and graphics by Sez, and released into the public domain sometime in 1991.

The cracking group Army of Darkness released a trained version on September 19, 2021

205707.overview:
Alpine Slopes (released in Italy under the  name Antica Arte dello Sci) is your typical 80s downhill skiiing game. There are no flags in this game, but you do have to avoid hitting the sides of the screen.

This was developed by Peter Gerrard and published by Duckworth Home Computing as a type-in program  in the book "Sprites & Sound on the Commodore 64" and by Jacopo Castelfranchi Editore (JCE) in the Italian translated version of the same book titled "Sprites & Suono del Commodore 64"

The italian version does have one minor difference, but that only difference being that it's played on a light grey background as opposed to the white background that is used in the English version.

205886.overview:
An Everyday Tale of a Seeker of Gold is a 2019 conversion of a 1986 ZX Spectrum text adventure of the same name. It was coded by John Wilson, who developed the original Spectrum version as well. The game itself is a parody of The 1982 adventure "The Hobbit", which of course is based on Tolkien's classic fantasy adventure novel of the same name. 

The game is part of what is known as "The Balrogian Trilogy".

206397.overview: Awari is a digital version of the game Kalah published in the book ""BASIC Computer Games - Microcomputer Edition".

206498.overview: Air-Command is a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up developed by Ryan Chenery using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. It was published by Binary Zone PD in 1993.

206700.overview: Animal Fare is an animal matching memory game for children. It was developed by Joel Epstein in 1990 and published in Loadstar #070. Test your speed and skill in remembering shapes and colors. A collection of 12 fun tests developed by a psychologist.

206725.overview:
The game is loosely (very loosely) based on 'Alien Research Centre 1 and 2. Initially created for the ZX Spectrum using the PunyInform platform which can create text adventures for multiple platforms. It was released as part of the "Pack of Three" multi-platform compilation. 

Introduction:
Last night's snowfall was heavy and as you enter the study you cannot help but notice the layers of snow on the frame and ledge of the window...

206818.overview:
Alpha Anxiety is a cross between an educational game and a board/memory game in which you have to find all 26  letters of the alphabet in order on the board. However unlike most memory games, the game is timed, so you only have a certain amount of time to find the letters.

The game was developed by Craig Howarth and published as a type-in listing in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/03 (Issue #21). It was also released in Italy by J.Soft s.r.l. in Super VIC & C64 A2-N10 (November 1985)

207290.overview:
Automata is a public domain life simulation for the Commodore 64. In the game, you raise/control single cell organisms (you can also raise DEMONS!). The game was developed and released by David Kinder in 1994.

The game is pretty much a variant of Conway's Game of Life, but with a few twists added.

207292.overview:
AngiePuffy Quest is a side scrolling platformer for the Commodore 64. It was developed by retrogamer1975 and released to the public domain in 2020. 

Story:

AngiePuffy lives on a small farm with her animals.  One day a gang of villains came and took all of them. Now she needs to find and save them before they are gone for good.

Collect all the keys you can find to open the locks holding them captive. All the keys on each level is needed to unlock it and rescue the animal.

207425.overview:
This is a traditional text adventure with 78 locations to visit and over 23 different objects to find. It is vert loosely based around several traditional tales.

Once upon a time, in a land far away, there lived an evil Ogre who delighted in terrorising the villagers. He would steal their sheep, rob their treasures and burn their houses to the ground. Your task is to visit the ogre's cottage when the ogre is away and recover the three items of treasure hidden there. Your task will not be easy, and you will need to kill the ogre when you have accomplished your task.

Published in Computer Gamer 1986/01 (Issue #10) as a type-in game.

207500.overview: AP is a Wild West-themed reaction game released for 1K Game Competition at 2002 MiniGame Compo. You need to "shoot" your opponents by pressing the corresponding letter that is visible on screen for a short time.

207501.overview: Ann Gong is a martial arts-themed fighting game that was released as an entry to the 4K competition at the 2005 MiniGame Compo.

207687.overview: Addy is a simple word guessing game for one player. it was developed by K. Lomax and self-published in 1983.

207716.overview:
While you shouldn't confuse Nibble Magazine's Adventure Writing System to the well-received The Quill: Adventure Writing System published year prior, it's quite likely that was exactly what the publisher was aiming for when choosing the name.

Originally released for Apple and then ported to multiple platforms including C64, 
Adventure Writing System let's you write your own text adventures. The program also features an unnamed text adventure (technically named "sample")  in which you're a knight on your way to kill a fire-breathing dragon in its lair.

207719.overview:
"From the Pine Tree state to the Golden gate, this program should appeal to anyone who wants to learn about the 50 states!"

This educational program will test your knowledge on US states, from state capitals to state flowers.

207828.overview: A keyboard controlled clone of Atari's Asteroids for the Commodore 64. This version was developed by David Rees and published in Your Commodore 1985/04.

207830.overview:
-"Ape want eat banana, but ape hate ant! Ape collect banana, but want avoid ant!"

Welcome to a super fast onebutton reaction game for the Commodore 64 made by the Megastyle team. 

"Apeshit" is a one button game where you jump from tree to tree while you try to avoid the scary insects. On the left tree Ape slides down the trunk, and on the right side ape climb up. Try to pick up bananas to gain extra points, but watch it so you dont jump into a branch while trying to pick it up.

Controls:
Plug a joystick in port 2 on your C64 and press fire to jump. This game is especially made to be used with the SIBUGA controller to get the ultimate one button experience.

Trainer:
The game has a built in trainer, you can activate it on the title screen by pressing F8. Note that once you have started the game with cheatmode activated, you will not get a save highscore

Credits:
Programmed by Docster
Coding help by Geir S. 
Graphics by Pixelburner
Music by Magnar
Loading music by Lukhash
Instructions Petscii by Rotteroy
Instructions viewer by Scroll
Testing by Endurion, Roysterini, Craig Derbyshire, Geir S, Rotteroy, Pixelburner and Docster.


So... Go ahead!! Go nuts!! GO APESHIT!!!

207838.overview:
Asteroid Lander is a lander game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Gary Leach and published in Your Computer 1984/03.

A Dutch version was also released by Courbois Software the same year.

207977.overview: Published in the book "Powerplays on the Commodore 64", Aggression is a political simulator. Watch the screen as nations build up their armies and declare war. Will the whole world go to war as rival ideologies collide or will peace and common sense prevail? Your computer becomes a test-tube of political power blocks - jealousy, greed, envy and mistrust - alliances and enemies - the far left versus the far right. Who will win? And why?

208008.overview: Antrock is a single player logical brain/puzzle game developed by Contrive Section in 1996. It was released on Loadstar #150.

208016.overview: Air Ball is a reaction game where your aim is to move your ball to the bottom by clicking fire to get through green and blue walls while avoiding red and yellow walls. Every time you clear one of the 24 levels you get your lost balls back.

208100.overview: Angels' Boulder Dash is a game made by Black and Index  using Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction Kit in 1998.

208101.overview: Angels' Boulder Dash II is the 2001 followup to Black and Index's Angels' Boulder Dash. However, Index was not involved in this sequel, instead a developer known as Hawk was Black's cohort in the sequel.

208117.overview: Abfahrer is a public domain German language stay-on-track racing game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Peter Diehm and released by PDPD Software in 1990. A very simple arcade game in which you must drive a vehicle that leaves tracks on the road without colliding with the edges of the road. To complete the game, you just need to survive for 59 seconds.

208118.overview: Arizona: The Boy in the Bubble Is a public domain German language selectable answers adventure game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Peter Diehm and published under his PDPD Software label in 1992.

208120.overview: Object of Plane is a simple shooter where your goal is to shoot the plane as many times as possible before it reaches the ground.

208132.overview: Published in a book "Farbspiele mit dem Commodore 64", Aktienbörse (Stock Exchabge) is a stock market simulation. You will start with $10K and end when you feel you're rich enough or have lost all your money.

208139.overview: On 6th of April 2180, a disaster happens when bacteria ALD-7 that was taken from Aldebaran System is accidentally set free in a bio lab. The lives of the nine scientists are in danger. The task of the player is - by using a remote-controlled robot - to bring the scientists into the upper right room and to avoid the spread of the free bacteria by sealing the lab rooms at seven places before the indicator at the upper rim of the screen reaches 100%. The less time one needs, the more points are given.

208442.overview: An adventure creation program converted for the C64 by David Turnbull from the Applesoft Program that first appeared in Nibble Magazine. With it, you can create exciting text adventures and share them with your friends!

208445.overview: Welcome! You have just been enlisted by the Governor to serve as a gladiator in the Arena of Death. You may select your own weapons and armor based on the scores you select for your Strength, Stamina and Sill. Your strength determines the amount of damage you are capable of inflicting. Skill is your ability to hit your opponent, while your own ability to survive being hit is reflected by your stamina. You may wear armor, but you will find that it hinders your fighting ability. You will have 100 points to assign to your attributes to start with.

208483.overview: From the group that brought you, My Balls are Dropping and PESCII Love comes Ahlienwahr Schuter! The name says it all. Shoot all the quickly advancing aliens before they get to you or you lose! Luckily, like in the martial arts movies, they only rush you one at a time!

208484.overview: Guide Tronic left and save Greenie Land. Avoid spikes and bash BadBots and pick up rings for more points in this Shoot'em Up Construction Set created horizontally scrolling shooter that came out in 2020.

208485.overview: A shooter created with the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit by TheReaperUK with music by Andrew Fisher. In it you must kill all the aliens and rescue any humans.

208576.overview: Alphanum Delight is an educational game for 1 player involving both letters and numbers. It was developed and published by Remsoft Systems in 1988. Part of the "Remsft Program Disk"

208657.overview: Not to be confused with another title called ALF that is about the alien from the 80s TV series, Alf is a space shooter made with the Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit SEUCK.

208794.overview:
A first attempt at C64 assembly language programming by Metesev aka MetaOne70. A simple shooter with borrowed sprites and music by Richard Bayliss. 

In this fixed shooter you are a lone starfighter and must destroy all the incoming alien ships that threaten mankind.

208887.overview:
A collection of previously released Activision titles, with added high scores that were not available during the original release. A disk version and an Easyflash cartridge version were released. 

Includes the following:
 
Chopper Command 
Keystone Kapers 
Frostbite 
Crackpots V1.01

209051.overview: One of the many type-in games simply called "Alien", your mission is to shoot the birds (aliens?) from the sky with your trusty tank. Origintally published in Homecomputer 1984/08, the game was later republished as "Invaders" in the "64'er Spielesammlung" magazine.

209052.overview: Yet another game simply called "Alien" for C64, the main feature that sets this shoot'em up apart from others is the size of sprites; you and your enemies are exceptionally big for a game of this type. Published in HC - Mein Home-Computer 1984/11.

209056.overview: Alien Attack is an adventure game where you play the captain of a space ship trying to get to your destination as fast as possible and especially before running out of fuel. In your way are numerous alien ships, sudden meteor showers and other random events. Do you raise your shields, do a scan, shoot a torpedo or escape to the hyper space? As the ship's captain the decision is yours.

209258.overview: Astray in Jungle is a public domain German language text adventure of unknown origin for the Commodore 64. Both the developer and year of release are unknown as of right now.

209291.overview:
You are Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, trapped in some parallel reality. Your mind is filled with musicians and your "Concerto in C".

Starting from the bottom you should break through to the top of your Sheet Music, which represents "Concerto in C". During your perilous travel, musicians of different kinds will want to kill you with the notes they've reproduced with their musical instruments. Each time the musician creates the note it is simulated with appropriate sound effect. You should avoid the notes and eliminate their sources gaining the points.

This game was released in the following:

-   Commodore 64 Club #05 [Italian Release]
-   Commodore Computer Club Nr.6 [v1]

209890.overview: Public domain Space Invaders clone for various systems released in 2020 by Marco Spedaletti aka spotlessmind1975 for the Retro Programmers Inside challenge. Versions were made for C64, Plus/4, C128 and Atari.

210291.overview: Released as part of the 2020 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition for Reset64 Magazine, in it James, who got seventh place out of almost 40 entrants, tries to create the best game possible in 4k of code or less. It is a rhythm based game where you need to avoid the blocks, jump over the red squares and collect the yellow dots.

210584.overview: An educational game created by Vince Apps and published in 1984 in the book "40 Educational Games for the Commodore 64". When you cover other sums programs in this book you will find that we recommend that you don’t use pencils, paper or calculators because you probably won’t have them the next time you are sent out to shop for your parents. It helps to be able to do your own sums in your head because it might save you having to go back to the shops because you didn’t have enough money the first time you went. We have made this game look just like it would on your school papers. You even fill in the totals by putting the numbers in from right to left just like you do in your math books. If you get a correct answer a little blue munchman will run across the screen and eat away the whole sum. If you are wrong however the munchman will only eat away the incorrect answer and you will have to try again. Give your munchman a full stomach by getting as many correct as you can because the score board will show how many tries and how many mistakes you made.

210641.overview: A Space Invaders clone by Jim Summers and released in 1983. In this game, the first shot will pop the eggs, so you can shoot the aliens that hatch out of them.

210643.overview: Set the gravity for your game and fuel up, blow up enemy helicopters and navigate your way into tight underground passages to save the Prisoners of War. I love the sound of choppers in the morning, it is the sound of victory! Game was published in multiple German language disk magazines including 64'er 1984/10, 64'er Sonderheft 1985/06, and 64'er Spielesammlung #2.

210649.overview:
Arcade Volleyball is a simple, two-player (human or computer) volleyball-like game where you have to, simply enough, bang the ball so that it hits the opposite player's ground. Some basic rules apply: when the ball's current owner loses a round (either because the ball touched the ground or he touched it for three times) the opposite player becomes the owner. If a player is not the owner of the ball and loses a round, the opposite player gains a point. The game is over when either player reaches 15 points.

The game was published in the following:

COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/06 (Issue #60), Best of Gazette 1988 (Disk Issue) / a 1-player option was added unofficially by the cracking group Army of Darkness in 2020.

210682.overview: Autorijden is a simple Dutch language overhead racing game for the Commodore 64. The game was developed and published by Courbois Software in 1984.

210736.overview: A remake of the original Aztec Challenge action game that was released in 1983, in this more BASIC version you still run towards the ziggurat while avoiding the spears thrown at you from the warriors forming the gauntlet that leads to the structure. Pull back on the stick to duck, push forward to jump the low spears. If you make it to the structure you must climb dangerous stairs and cross the deadly bridge.

210759.overview:
A Bee C's is an educational game for little children. It teaches the alphabet by using a hardware speech module addon (Magic Voice) for the C64. You can either learn the letters or play a game where you have to find the correct letters.

This was only one of three programs released that supported Commodore's Magic Voice Speech module, the other two being GORF, and Wizard of Wor.

210797.overview: Airfight is a 2 player only 1 on 1 duel style airplane shooter in which the first person to reach a certain amount of "kills" first is the winner. The game was developed by Mario Walther, however the year of release is currently unknown.

211248.overview: Amaurote is a classic title that many of you would remember from ZX Spectrum or Atari 800 developed by Ste and John Pickford. The C64 version was a different looking game, not using the isometric view and roughly based on the Amaurote concept, with one of the few common factors with the original was the music by David Whittaker, which, unfortunately, did not leverage the C64's amazing music capabilities (although it is stylish and creepy).

211249.overview: A great looking game in similar style to the first part of Dinamic’s "Game Over", with some awesome graphics in similar style to those common with X-Ample games of the early 90’s. This game is not based on any moon landings or space trips, but of a space man who roams around various flick-screen colourful rooms of shooting pods and robots, all of which animate beautifully. Not only that, but the main character is well defined with a hi-res overlay and great animation. Only released as preview, full game never released.

211274.overview:
Ahh, the local arcade. How many hours did we spend glued to the screen and  How many coins did we chuck into them?
 
But how many did you complete? Was there always the same name at the top of the highscore you could never beat?
 
Welcome to Arcade Daze, the best arcade in town!
 
Can you be the new coolest kid in town and complete every arcade game?
 
Can you take the crown away from the legendary Kelly and the pusspuss gang?

The game basically consists of the main game which you have to go around collecting coins and avoiding Kelly and her cat(s), then there are several mini-games to spend the coins on, all of which are clones of classic arcade games such as Frogger, Pac-Man, and Space Invaders.

The game was created as a tribute to C64 classic, Lazy Jones.

211308.overview:
Aicd Rain is a text adventure for several personal computers, as it was written in Infocom Z-Code, which means it can easily be ported to various computers. This was the version ported to the C64 in the same year that the original was written.

Introduction:

You were driving home from the Second National Conference on Acid Rain when you started getting tired. As it was late at night, and you were in the middle of nowhere, you pulled over to the side of the road for a bit of shut-eye.

When you wake up, you find that it's dark and dismal outside and raining heavily. You'd better get a move on and get the car under cover. Despite all the protective coating you've applied, acid rain can still make a mess of your duco.

Goal:

Your goal is to start the car and drive home. You will soon find that this is not as easy as it sounds. As the story develops, you will find that there are multiple sub-goals. I can't tell you what they are, as that would spoil the fun.
Instructions

This is a traditional text adventure that was written for ParserComp 2021.

A text adventure is a form of computer game that presents you with a story. You take on the role of the main character in the story and control that character's actions. The story has a goal, and you will need to solve puzzles in order to achieve that goal. The computer tells you where you are, what you can see and what's happening around you. You can then move around, examine the things you find, and manipulate those things by telling the computer what to do using simple English commands.

Commands consist of a verb phrase, optionally followed by a noun phrase. Most commands can be abbreviated to a verb followed by a noun. For example, START THE CAR can be abbreviated to START CAR.

In some cases, the verb phrase and first noun phrase may be followed by a second noun phrase. The two noun phrases are usually separated by a preposition. For example, UNLOCK GATE WITH IRON KEY. If you only use a verb and a noun, the game will generally tell you if it needs an extra phrase or implicitly try to deduce what is needed for the second phrase.

Don't panic! It's not as complicated as it sounds. Just use simple English sentences starting with a verb, and it will all feel quite natural.

Movement:

To move around, use commands like GO NORTH and WALK SOUTH. You can move in any of the four cardinal compass directions, as well as UP and DOWN. (There are no diagonal directions in this game.) To save typing, movement commands can be abbreviated to N, S, E, W, U and D. You can sometimes use other movement commands such as CLIMB, ENTER, EXIT, GET ON, GET OFF and JUMP. Most of these are alternatives to normal compass directions. There is only one exception, and this will be reasonably obvious when the time comes.

Whatever you do, make sure you draw a map as you go. This is a medium-sized game. If you don't draw a map, you will most certainly get lost or miss exits to other locations.

211309.overview:
Avon is an unofficial conversion of a text adventure that was released on several computers back in the 80s, such as the BBC Micro, Spectrum, and MS-DOS based computers.

It was never officially released on the Commodore 64. The game was made with Infocom's Zcode engine. The game was converted to run on the C64 by an unknown person in 2021 using the online zcode compiler, Ozmoo Online, which essentially just makes it a ROM hack.

Game description:

Avon is an appropriately Shakespearean adventure which beings innocently enough, with a sight-seeing visit to the celebrated playwright's hometown. As the protagonist explores the streets and souvenir shops, certain people, animals and objects begin exhibiting strange behavior; finally, the surroundings become completely unfamiliar, and the inhabitants' English unusually rich and poetic... the stage is set for an exploration of this strange land, in an attempt to find a way out. The happenings take place over three different calendar dates; the game world is a blend of places and characters from Shakespeare's plays, but as the authors reassure us, "an exhaustive knowledge of the Shakespearean Canon is not necessary".

211323.overview: Climber is a 1983 C64 game heavily inspired by the arcade game Crazy Climber. It was developed by Australian based coder Terry Mason and originally published by Computer Classics Pty. It was later released in Europe a year later, however the publisher is not known, and the name was changed to Ape Escape.

211445.overview: Arachnia 64 is a 1986 shooter in which the player controls a spider trying to protect his/her web from other enemy spiders. The game was developed by Sean D. Wagle and published in Loadstar #22.

212961.overview:
In this game, with some similarities to games like Dig Dug, you play a farmer that must protect his farm from evil mutated cabbages. Spray your water hose at the cabbages to take them out.

The game was programed by Anthony Stiller, while Vanja J. Utne did the music and SFX. The game was released into the public domain in 2016.

212965.overview:
Agent 101... That's you of course has been sent to the French Alps in order to fight against an agents' henchmen. Ski through each level, shooting away the bad guys. Can you do it? ... Well if you don't you will be a failure :)

The game was developed by Roberto Ricioppo using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit and released on TND in 2016.

213355.overview:
Adept: Space Waste 2 (also known as Adept: Space Waste II) is the followup to Alan Bond's 1985 game Space Waste. This time however, the game has more variety, as there is different types of enemies to kill, and unlike Space Waste, this game has joystick support. The game plays similar to Space Invaders or Galaxian. 

Every wave features the same enemy like in the original, except the enemies change from wave to wave. So instead of facing diamond shaped spaceships in every wave, you end up facing a typical space invader in one wave, and the next wave you're facing asteroids, etc.

213360.overview:
Garten Eden (also released in The Netherlands as Appel Vangen) is a German language "catch it" game similar to games like Kaboom. Except this time, you play a farmhand who must catch the apples falling from the tree. Misd too many, and you will be fired.

Originally published in Happy Computer 1984/07. Then released by Courbois Software in Courbois Software #6430

213376.overview: Android is a single screen platformer for the Commodore 64. It has some similarities to games like Lode Runner and Jump Man. It was developed by Marcus "Lost Brain" Hinzmann and released into the public domain in 1999

213649.overview: Alchemist is a puzzle game similar to games like Columns for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Davide Gessa and released into the public domain in 2021.

213704.overview:
Anna's Gram is a 1987 anagram themed word game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Mike Maynard and published in This game was a recurring feature on several of Softdisk's disk subscriptions; each time it appeared on a particular platform, it contained different puzzles. It's a combination word game/sliding tile puzzle in which letters must be manipulated and rearranged within a constrained area in order to spell out words. Several words can be worked on simultaneously, and the letters that appear in the last word of each set are determined by the positions of the letters in earlier words.

The C64 version was developed by Mike Maynard and published in Loadstar #043.

213920.overview:
Programming: Roberto Ricioppo (Using Sideways S.E.U.C.K)
Graphics: Roberto Ricioppo
Music: Richard Bayliss
Genre: Shoot 'Em Up (S.E.U.C.K)
Tape Loader: Thunderload (Richard Bayliss + Martin Piper)
Year of release: 2016

Deep under the ocean lies a secret underground lair. You are a diver, who has been assigned a mission in which is to find that hidden lair and clean out the sea from mutant fish and rogue objects. In order to do this, you must shoot away at the objects. Try to avoid getting caught. If you get caught your diving suit will get destroyed. Good luck.

214160.overview:
Algol is vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by playOrbit as part of the 2018 SEUCK competition.

Control the Orbis aka "The Harvester of Doom," from the Soros System. Invade, subjugate and destroy the planet of Eden. There are 10 levels in total.

214183.overview:
Not to be confused with Airborne Ranger from Microprose Software, Airborne Rangers from Bombjack Ltd. is a 1988 SEUCK game for 1 or 2 players (Co-Op).

In this Commando style shooter, you must wipe out all the enemeis before they wipe you out.

214184.overview:
Alphafighter is a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Ghosthuntersoft using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1990. 

It is actually a hacked version of another SEUCK game called Stormtrooper, which was initially released in 1988.

214279.overview: All Stars is a vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. The game can be played with 1 or 2 players (co-op play)It was developed by Keith Killilea (also known Knightcoder) using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1998.

214865.overview: A worm game created in a moment of madness by XL of Xlcus Software and Design in October of 1995. Like other worm games, grab the treat without hitting the walls or yourself. You'll get bigger with each treat!
