214866.overview: An Italian text adventure with graphic pictures crated by Alessandro Zanello  and released in 1986 in Next Strategy n.10 (07/1986). Part of the Alberto Sorrio multi-game series.

214867.overview: An Italian language text adventure withe Hi-Res art game created by Alessandro Zanello as part of the Alberto Sorrio game series. It was published in Next Strategy n.08 (05/1986)

214868.overview:
A single player, selectable answers text adventure written by Wilfried Elmenreich & Woz of Vintage Computing Carinthia and released in 2020. Alice - Escape from Wonderland is a game where you control Alice through a part of Wonderland trying to find things that help you escape. The game is a "Walk-and-Click" adventure.

You can use WASD or a joystick to walk around. The cursor keys are used to move the inventory carousel (once you have multiple items there). The keys T,U,O,P,M,G,L are for selecting an interaction with objects, Return confirms it.

214869.overview: A science fiction text adventure created with the Graphic Adventure Creator (GAC) by Mark R. Turner and published originally in 1987. The updated 1989 edition appeared on the June 1989 edition of Commodore Disk User and the game also appeared on the covertape of Your Commodore March 1991. You come to after a great battle in space, can you avoid the security beams, avoid getting sucked into space and the enemy Drygars and rescue your ship, the Astrodeus?

214870.overview: A German language adventure role playing game created by Gordon Axmann in 1987.

214871.overview: Created by Liam O'Connor. Initially released in the Windows/MacOS/Linux compilation "Micro Entertainment Pack" in 2020. Later ported to 6502 based machines, this included the C64 and C16 too. This game is a minesweeper variant where you can choose the board size, the difficulty, use the cursor keys to move, space to dig and Enter\Return to put up a flag.

215029.overview:
Add and Subtract is an educational math game for the Commodore 64. It was published by Vision Software, however the year of release is not currently known,

The game has four modes:

1. Basic Addition - simple addition problems
2. Basic Subtraction - simple subtraction problems
3. Addition - more advanced addition problems
4. Subtraction - more advanced subtraction problems

216882.overview: Al*Bert! is a clone of Q*Bert for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Derek and released as part of Reset Magazine's 2020 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition.

216893.overview: Ascenseurs is a keyboard controlled single-screen platformer from France. It was developed by Eric Ravis and released as a type-in game in the book "Commodore 64 - Jeux d'Action" in 1985.

217593.overview: A German language, selectable answers text adventure game created by Maik Holstein and published in 1997 by B-Soft. The title means On or Onwards to Thordan.

217671.overview:
In this simple single-key shooter, your goal is to destroy as many enemy submarines with your plane as you can, until you have to return to your home base after all your fly-bys run out.

This game was developed by OnlineProf2010 and released into the public domain on October 5, 2014.

217673.overview:
Alien Blitz is a simple space shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Simon Jones using G-Pascal and published in Australian Commodore Review 1984/06.

Game description:

A single alien flies down the screen at a time. The player has to shoot and kill the aliens as they advance. The alien increases in speed as the game progresses, which increases the challenge. The alien itself does not actually shoot. If the alien touches the player's ship or the bottom of the screen, the game is over.

Uses simple black and white graphics

218787.overview: Arms is a 1-4 player pinball game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Puma Rock using Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Construction Set. It was released on Pcs Club Disk #31 in 1991.

218954.overview: A new Commodore 64 game which is based around the ColecoVision version from Xonox! Artillery Duel Deluxe is one of many games in the genre of "turn-based artillery games". Such games are among the earliest computer games, with versions existing for mainframes with only teletype output. Scorched Earth, with a plethora of weapon types and power-ups, is considered the modern archetype of its format. Also all weapons are shown with tracers which allow the player to more accurately adjust the trajectory on their next turn! Works with the WiC64 for online modes, duels with online players, watch online games and online leader board. Choose your grade for game difficulty: Private, Captain or General and gain rank as you play.

218997.overview: Argon is a single-player vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Helmut Wegener using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and was released as part of Digital Marketing PD #88.

218998.overview: The Armageddon Files is a single-player run and gun style vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Cyber Systems using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and published by Binary Zone PD in 1995.

219316.overview:
You are a star ranger deployed for long range reconnaissance mission in Rimward asteroid belt where Megacorp has eight Verge stations for asteroid mining. Suddenly your Long Range Quantum Communication link flashes and you receive new mission:
STATUS REPORT
=============
ROSCOS TERRORIST CELL HAS CAPTURED RESEARCH STATION 
TO HARNESS CORE DENSITY SINGULARITY AND ASSURE 
UNLIMITED ENERGY SOURCE AND WORLD DOMINATION
+
WARNING!
========
PROJECTIONS INDICATE POSSIBILITY OF RUNAWAY SINGULARITY
RESULTING IN SUPERCLUSTER DESTRUCTION
+
MISSION
=======
TO BUILD A SINGULARITY DIFFUSER YOU MUST ACQUIRE
 - NEUMAN BINDER
 - BABBAGE SIPHON
 - LAPLACE REACTOR
 - FERMI ENTANGLER
+
INTELLIGENCE REPORTS THAT LISTED COMPONENTS 
ARE AVAILABLE IN NEARBY VERGE STATIONS
+
NEGOTIATE WITH SPACE STATIONS AND GET THE PARTS BEFORE RUNAWAY SINGULARITY DESTROYS SPACETIME 
 
There are no other ships within jump distance to assist - you are on your own! When game stars, your ship is located in Verge Station 5 and you will get your mission briefing via long range quantum communication link.

219317.overview:
Unlike most other games made with the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, this is not a shooter. Instead, it's a general avoid and jump game, in which you play a penguin that got lost from the rest of his family. Can you make it back to your family, and avoid the baddies?

Developed by Igor Errazkin and released as part of the 2016 SEUCK Competition.

219407.overview:
My name is Frank Further. Further... It’s kind of ironic, come to think of it, as I’ve never left my village. Neither had my dad and his dad before him. It’s the same for everyone in our land since our four statues of wellness were stolen one night moons ago. Everyone seems to be cursed with numbness, immobility, and indifference. Adventure, curiosity, audacity and courage are words that have disappeared from our vocabulary.

I was born in Porkville and, as sure as the gods made little green apples, I know I’m going to die in Porkville. Without ever leaving the valley. Oh, don’t get me wrong. It’s a nice and pleasant lowland with green pastures, fruit trees, wild mushrooms, flowers and a beautiful little pond.
The only thing that disturbs the peace of this little haven are the mosquitoes and the fireflies. I hate these stupid insects and I sometimes chase them. I have to be thankful to them though as it is during one of my mundane bug hunts that I stumbled upon the entrance to a cave... Could this be my quest? A pig quest?

Experience one of the most incredible stories ever told on the Commodore 64: 5 large worlds to explore, hundreds of enemies, and 30+ epic SID tunes that appear dynamically in this action-packed platformer with puzzle elements intelligently woven in as the story unfolds.

219427.overview: Aliens are invading Earth!!!!..... again... A group of courageous spacemen has been sent to reject the attack, but the last chance for mankind is in your hands. You, a brave pilot, has been recluted to control ARCOS, the ultra-secret ultimate weapon. Your mission, easy to understand but hard to achieve: Kill the aliens and save the spacemen. With the power of ARCOS lead us to the victory!!! Your mission is to kill all aliens on the screen and save many spacemen as possible. You control ARCOS, a spaceship which bounces an energy ball that destroys everything in its path. If you miss the ball, you lose one life; you begin with 5 lives. In addition, ARCOS has a laser blast with limited ammo. Initially, you've got 10 shoots, but you can get extra ammo when you clear a stage, depending on the number of spacemen you've saved. Use this weapon with caution... it's limited and it can kill spacemen too.

219688.overview:
Area 13 is a 2 player duel shoot 'em up game for the Commodore 64. In the game, you and your opponent are both on jetpacks in the middle of space. Unlike most games of this type, instead of having to reach a certain set score, the goal is to be the first to not run out of energy.

However, there is a twist to this game: not only do you (or the AI player as well) have to deal with each other's bullets, they also have to contend with flying space rocks that can also deplete your energy, also hitting the pink/magenta colored force fields at the bottom and top of the screen result in an INSTANT loss of game for a player. Good luck!

The game was developed by Hans-Werner Müller and published in 1993 in the following:

•  64'er 1991/03
•  64'er Sonderheft 79

219912.overview:
Despite it's name, this is NOT a ROM hack of Arkanoid, rather it's a ROM hacked version of a game called Block-Out, which was only officially released as a magazine game in 64'er 1985/11, and 64'er Spielesammlung #2. 

This is just a standard Breakout clone, originally only released in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, under it's original Block-Out name.

219969.overview: An avoid-it action game for two (only), created by Phil64 and released for the CSDb C64 Fun Compo 2021. Avoid everything. Survive as long as possible.

379801.overview:
BBC Ask the Family is a 2 player only educational quiz game based on the British game show that ran from Jun 12, 1967 to October 22, 1984.

The game was developed and published by Ivan Berg Software in 1984.

417649.overview:
A game created by Victor Barbee and published in the ReRun Special Summer Edition 1990.  
 
DOG-GONE IT! This could be a real cat-astrophe. The city is in an uproar as canines and felines batte for dominance. That's the scene in Alley Wars, a C-64 game designed for two, three or four players. The battleground covers nine neighborhoods of nine blocks each. Wide boulevards separate the neighborhoods, with a single block at each intersection.
The combatants are divided into four squads: two cat squads, represented on the board by red and purple, and two dog squads, represented by green and yellow. As top cat or top dog you must lead your charges to occupy a horizontal, vertical or diagonal line of three blocks within a neighborhood or across an intersection— and prevent opposing squads from doing the same. Blocks you occupy become your squad's color.

When four people play, each commands one cat squad or one dog squad. When two play, the first person commands both cat squads and the second both dog squads, but a winning line can still consist of only one color. When three people play, they don't have specific squads and can win with any color.
Alley Wars is played with either a single joystick in port 2 or joysticks in both ports 1 and 2. The red cat squad goes first. As its commander, use the joystick to position the white frame over the desired block and press the fire button. The block will become yours and change to your squad's color. You can't claim blocks that are already occupied.

As soon as you've claimed a block, game control passes to the next squad. When a squad succeeds in forming a three-block line, a winning fanfare sounds, the border color changes and the game ends. To start another game, press the fire button.

Alley Wars is somewhat similar to tic-tac-toe, but unlike tic-tac-toe the block arrangements and playing strategies seem endless. When you command two squads, often one can be used for diversion as the other executes a complex and hopefully subtle offensive move.

417859.overview: A party game by up to four players (with 4 player adapter) by Torsten Baade (Edikles) and released at the BBC Party #03 in 2009.

417884.overview: In this odd take on games like Kaboom, your goal is either to drop a deuce in the toilet on the bottom of the screen, or to play as the toilet and catch the turds as they fall. The game was developed by Sasha Stojanovic and released into the public domain in 2011.

417981.overview: Cute collect em up created by R. Pahmeyer & John Bettels with a song you don't hear much these days. It was published in Input 64 1985/07. Joy Stick artistry is more important in this game than good nerves and overview. only marginally asked In detail: After the successful passage through the seventh picture you expect "Congratulations". In each picture you have to reach the phone to advance. The way there is lined with permanent loss of energy. Your starting supply of 64 energy units is reduced by touching the apples, the walls and not by pressing the spacebar - opened doors. The bar at the top left of the screen shows the current energy supply. You can get refills by touching the worm. The unused energy is taken over into the High Score section. If you ever get to this stage: you can enter your name by selecting the letters with the keys "a", "d", "*" and "/" or the space bar (as an acknowledgment), and in the second pass ( after the "Congratulations"), the initial energy is reduced by a quarter. The f1 button takes you back to the menu.

419006.overview:
The Anglers is a 2 player only competitive action game for the Commodore 64, in which you and a friend try to catch the most fish. The winner is whoever catches the most fish after a set score. You can change the difficulty by adding boats and other sea critters that can get in your wey.

The game was developed by Tai Bush and published in the March 1989 issue of COMPUTE!'S Gazette (Issue #69).

419243.overview:
Blackbeard the Pirate (also known as The Adventures of Blackbeard) is a text adventure with selectable answers for the C64.

In this swashbuckling adventure, you play the infamous Blackbeard on a search for treasure.

The game was developed by Phil Wulf and published by Compu-Story in 1985.

419915.overview: Adventure System is a program in which the user can create their own text adventure games for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jörg Walkowiak. It was originally published in Germany by Data Becker in the book  "Adventures - und wie man sie programmiert" and then was translated to English and published in 1985 by Abacus Software in the book  "Adventure Gamewriter's Handbook for Commodore 64". Despite this, the title screen for the North American release still says 1984.

420780.overview:
To humans of the far future, the forgotten planet Earth is nothing but an old tale. That is, until a lucky explorer stumbles into the lost blue sphere... but will signs of ancient habitation be found? It's time to break out your three trusty Archeodroids - excavation robots programmed to retrieve archeological evidence. Their job? - to poke around in Earth's garbage, and retrieve the debris that holds the key to mankind's past: human skeletons, car debris and piles o' junk.
 

Points are earned by bringing dug-up artifacts to the ship; each droid is equipped with ten power charges, allowing it to move and blast through the dirt. Trouble is, a chargeless droid will quickly self-destruct unless it recharges back at the ship - plus, cave-ins may block up the tunnels and even destroy the poor droid. A deceased droid's remains (and its collected artifacts) can be picked up by its successor. Your objective is to plan your excavations carefully, avoid getting trapped, and receive the maximum score for your findings.
 
Game published in Home Computer Magazine Vol.5, No.4.

421368.overview:
Affili8! was developed for the annual Mini Game Competition and was an entry for the 2k size category.

A clone of Pipe Dream, Affili8! is a puzzle game where the point is to build a network of pipes so that a marble can pass through it without crashing into the walls, the sides of pipes or falling into the void.

You can set up a pipe fragment somewhere in the 6x6 playfield by moving the cursor with your joystick and pressing Fire. On the right side of the screen, you see the pipe fragment which you are now placing; once you place it, a new, random one is chosen. Sometimes you'll get a bomb instead, which can destroy a single tile on the playfield. You have 5 seconds to place a tile (or a bomb) - if you wait too long, you lose one of four possible "misses"; when you lose them all, it's game over. When a marble passes through a pipe tile, this tile disappears.

The player receives a point for each placed tile, and 10 points when the marble passes through the pipes and reaches the checkered flag outside the playfield. Note that once the marble passes the flag, it will continue to roll through a small corridor outside the playfield and towards the entrance to the playfield again, so the game can be continued indefinitely.

421652.overview:
A Week That Changed the World is the second game in Series 2 of the Baker Street Kids franchise, with stories written by father/son duo V. Gilbert Beers and Ronald Beers. It consists of 14 Bible stories, starting with Jesus' triumphant entry into Jerusalem, going through Holy Week to the Passion of the Lord, and ending with the death of Judas Iscariot.

After selecting one of fourteen stories, you are given a choice of one of three difficulty levels: Tough, Very Tough, or Super Tough. For each story selection, you get to read the story (some of them riddled with typos and some inaccuracies in Bible translation), and then answer several questions about it, consisting of choosing one of three options. Frequently the questions will be true or false questions, but because there are three options, one option will be "who knows?", "doesn't say", "maybe", "don't know", etc. -- which is guaranteed to be wrong. Once you get at least most of the answers right, you are treated to a little light animation.

421714.overview:
Aerial is part of a series of games by Japanese developer Inufuto, who builds a single game design and then ports it to a very wide variety of retro hardware.

Aerial is a side-scrolling shooter, in which the player pilots a plane viewed from the side-scrolling left to right. The joystick is used to pitch the plane up or down, and fire button to fire. The objective is to avoid planes/rockets being launched at the player, and shoot down planes or ground targets when possible. Powerups will also appear that are used by flying over them.

421823.overview:
Alien Invaders: Plus! (also spelled without the separator) is an unofficial conversion of the Magnavox Odyssey 2 game of the same name for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Second Dimension and released into the public domain on June 30, 2023.

Game description: 

This is a Space Invaders variant with a twist. Eight robots with laser cannons and protected by a shield wall are advancing in the player's sector, and with his laser cannon he has to destroy them. The shield wall is indestructible, but the robots and the cannons aren't. They'll go from side to side of the screen in an alternate movement, shooting down. Three high density molecular laser shields are placed in defense of the laser cannon. Each one of them houses an extra cannon.

Instead of a passing flying saucer as seen in Space Invaders, the player has to face the Merciless Monstroth, which shoots against him. The player controls a robot defender inside the laser cannon. If the laser cannon is destroyed, the robot will be left unprotected. The robot can enter a new laser cannon housed in one of the shields. Once the new laser cannon is active, the shield is gone. Once the three shields are gone, the Merciless Monstroth will come down to hunt the player's cannon and robot.

The player wins a battle when destroying all enemy robots and cannons on the screen. A battle is lost when the player's robot is destroyed. The first side to win ten battles wins the war.

422484.overview:
Aztec Tomb is Georg's entry for the Retro Platform Jam #6.

Theme is "Underground". You explore an underground aztec tomb, looking for an ancient relic. Survive cunning puzzles and traps.

Unfortunately, the entry currently has a measly 8 stages, but hopefully there'll be more!

In game press Run/Stop to restart a stage if you get stuck!

422886.overview: Attack of the Slime Creatures is a single button (space bar) shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Joseph C. Giarratano and published by Que in the book "Time Lost" in 1984.

423928.overview: Somewhat uninspired but smooth shooter from the book "Best Of PCW: Software For The Commodore 64".

423934.overview: Alien Terrordome is an unreleased co-op shmup for two players.

423937.overview:
Alien Snipers is a reaction/typing game published in a book "Computer Spacegames". 

After selecting the difficulty, your computer will print a letter and a number. You must think through the alphabet by that number of letters and type in the letter you get to. E.g. for M 4, you must type Q, and for C 2, you must type E and so on. Typing in a letter automatically triggers off your laser gun, so if your letter is correct you'll score a hit. You get 10 alien snipers each game.

423944.overview: Alien Storm is a simple shooter, published as a type-in game in Vince Apps' "The Commodore 64: Program Book"-

423952.overview: Alien Invader is an ascii shooter where, instead of two cowboys, two aliens duke it out in a fast draw-style shootout.

423962.overview: Alien Patrol consists of two phases: In first, you'll scroll the screen to find the alien. Once you do, you need to stun it by shooting at it FPS-style. Once you accomplish that, you move to the second phase where you'll fly a helicopter above it, catch it to your net and ship it to safety.

423964.overview: In Alien Sounds, keys 1-8 work as a piano. After repeating a tune correctly, the alien ship moves towards the ground. The goal is to get the ship to land safely.

424170.overview: Action Maze Chase is a maze/labyrinth game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Josip Kalebic and released for free in 2022.

424730.overview: By controlling a combat helicopter equipped with a gun and bombs, you must destroy ground and air targets. The helicopter takes off from a sea landing pad to recharge bombs and repair damage. The player's task is to destroy six factories and four strategic, mostly moving targets with bombs. You need to drop several or even a dozen bombs on one factory to destroy it. As you progress, the number of enemy units increases and planes and bombers appear from time to time, attacking the player's landing site. The destruction of the landing site cannot be allowed at all costs.

424795.overview: The player's task is to collect all the keys from an underground complex full of traps and find the exit.

424815.overview: The player takes on the role of Santa Claus distributing gifts dropped by angels. There are two types of package distribution in the game - dropping them down the chimney and personally placing a gift under the Christmas tree. In the latter case, the player will have to avoid meeting flames in the chimney and people wandering around the house at night. After leaving the gifts and taking the key, you can head for the exit. During the flight, a collision with any object results in the loss of one of the captured packages, and a collision with lightning unfortunately ends tragically.

424817.overview: The player's task is to fly to the other side of the cave trying not to touch any obstacle.

424828.overview: The player's task is, with the help of a fighter plane, to defend four cities from alien attack. To do this, in addition to shooting down alien vehicles, you still need to replenish the cities' energy by drawing power from nearby generators. Driving alien vehicles can be destroyed by dropping bombs on them.

424943.overview: The player's task is to collect all the marbles found in a huge cave complex full of deadly traps and reach the place where the big cup stands. While wandering, you need to collect keys to open passages to the next areas. You can only carry one key at a time.

424952.overview: The game is divided into four stages. In the first, you have to avoid colliding with other traffic participants until the distance bar reaches zero. In the second stage, you have to eliminate a sufficient number of enemies with your gun. The third stage involves talking to a woman and finally the fourth stage, in which you must defeat your opponent in hand-to-hand combat.

424990.overview: The player finds himself in a maze of endless rooms guarded by soulless robots. To defend against them, you use fired projectiles. In some rooms there is a bonus item to take. Over time, after reaching a certain number of points, the number of robots will begin to increase. All walls are live so do not touch them. Staying in one room for too long will activate the indestructible flying robot, and if this happens, leave the danger area as soon as possible.

425035.overview: The evil telemaniac from the first part was not defeated (black scenario) and threw the agent into a large maze. The player's task is to find the exit before the points reach zero. An additional complication is the live walls.

425037.overview:
The player's task is to shoot at everything that appears on the screen while avoiding being hit by enemy bullets.

A Norwegian 1-2 player cooperative SEUCK GAME developed by Reinhart Olsen.

425039.overview: The player is tasked with protecting the city from attack by enemy drones. At the beginning, fuel and ammunition are refueled on the platform and after they are loaded, the attack is launched. It is good to wait until the planes fly over and attack them from behind. From time to time, refuel by landing on platforms that have not yet been destroyed. As you progress, more and more planes arrive.

425046.overview: The player's task is to shoot down all drones and helicopters while trying not to be hit by a bomb.

425054.overview:
The player takes on the role of Agent 000 and drives a high-tech vehicle that turns into a boat when it reaches the water. The vehicle is equipped with bombs and surface-to-air missiles. Weapons are generally needed to light up the sky when hit by a flying diamond, so that unlit objects like oil towers at sea can be seen. Bombs, on the other hand, illuminate what is underwater. Everything else is invulnerable to the player's projectiles. In addition to driving and swimming, the vehicle can also perform the high jumps necessary to avoid obstacles and holes in the ground.

This is an Italian bootleg of the first James Bond C64 game, which was released way back in 1983.

425058.overview:
The player has four competitions to play that test strength, dexterity, speed and memory. A maximum of 250 points can be earned in each of these competitions. After completing all the tests, the player's score and ranking will appear on the screen.

Published in 64'er Software Extra Nr.20: Spiele.

425073.overview: Agent Rod is on a very tough mission. An evil spy is smuggling armed supplies to his hideout, and is willing to secretly sell those to the criminals who, now own them. He hears of an undercover agent (that's you, Agent Rod) coming his way, and decides to send out his forces to fight against you. This won't be any normal and simple chase, as all the enemies are after you by land, and also by sea. Can you battle against the enemies, and finally reach his hideout, or will you 'die another day?

425078.overview: The player's task is to land the balloon safely at the airport while avoiding collision with white dots and a flying missile. The balloon has a certain amount of fuel, which is consumed while flying upwards. In order to land it is necessary to reduce the speed accordingly, otherwise the balloon will crash.

425099.overview:
The player's task, within a certain time limit, is to place the cars in a three-story garage in the spaces corresponding to their numbers.

Released in Next Game #02 (10/1984)

425112.overview: The player's task is to land on one of three platforms and take Alfredo home. Each platform has a multiplier that increases 2x, 3x or 4x the amount of points you have. When landing, watch out for asteroids and enemy creatures. The game has a time limit, after which it permanently ends.

425116.overview: A classic shooter in which you have to eliminate landing aliens. If at least one of them lands, the game is over.

425120.overview: The player's task is to collect twigs and make a nest out of them on the tree before time runs out. Twigs can be found on a busy street so avoid vehicles or eliminate them by dropping droppings on them. While flying, you can catch butterflies and you should avoid the orange bird, which will precipitate the twig carried by the albatross. After completing the task, the difficulty level increases and new dangerous objects like an airplane appear.

425124.overview: The player's task is to shoot down all the blocks on the board while avoiding contact with the falling alien. From some of the destroyed blocks a question mark falls out, after collecting which you can gain more powerful weapons, acceleration, extra energy, reversal of directions, etc.

425141.overview: Players control paddles and bounce the puck setting it in motion at different speeds and directions. A point is reached when the puck hits the player's or opponent's goal. The game ends after a certain amount of time or when one player reaches the maximum number of points.

425148.overview: By jumping and moving left and right, the player's task is to traverse all parts of the castle wall, being careful not to fall or be knocked down by moving objects.

425178.overview: 1 of 2 games called Alienator for the Commodore 64. This is a vertically scrolling shooter made by Bad Boys Productions using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit. It has 1-2 players (co-op). The game was released in 1994.

425182.overview: You are a pilot who was going to land safely to see you family. Unfortunately, your air port has been invaded by illegal smugglers. Your mission is to clear the airways by blasting out the enemy planes, so you can return back to your base and make a safe landing. Good luck pilot.

425195.overview:
1 of 2 games called Alienator for the Commodore 64. This one is a 1-player fixed screen shooter similar to games like Space Invaders. It was developed by Georg Rottensteiner with extra development by Hugo Hoekstra. It was released into the public domain in 2016.

Originally released as part of RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2015/2016. Later released as part of Reset #09 Mix-i-Disk from Reset64 Magazine.

425243.overview:
Accuse, by David A. Wheeler, converted to the C64 by MGProduction and Marco Giorgini in particular. It is a  (vaguely) Cluedo-like replayable game. 

A murder, in a mansion, with three suspects, three potential murder weapons, and five locations, and you, a detective with "powers", able to understand if a specific accusation is correct or not.

Being each play based on a random selection, you could play this game more than once, even if (as even the original author admitted) this is more a logical puzzle game than a mystery game (so the environment is just "for fun" than something you need to analyze).

Anyway, the game is free, the source code is available, and I guess that my Accuse release could be worth a try if you're into this kind of game :-)

Some basic instructions (available also in-game)

- your goal is to find who's the murderer, which weapon he/she used, and in which room he/she committed the crime. To find that you rely solely on your accusation abilities - that will give you implicit hints, telling you if your accusation is completely wrong, or if partially wrong.

- your accusation must include the suspect, the weapon, and the location. Location is *implicit* (you must be in a location to accuse someone to have killed the victim there) so you must invite the suspect there. You need to have there the weapon too, but you can pick it up and have it with you, so that's easier. Accusation is done writing "accuse suspect with weapon"

- in the original game each accusation must be completely different from the previous one (you can't accuse the same person twice in a row, nor use the same weapon, or the same place). I made my game a bit simpler, removing the each-time-a-different-place part (you don't need to change also the location from one accusation and the next one)

425246.overview: A prototype shooter which involves the Amiga ball.

425249.overview:
Ascend is a platform game where the objective is to reach the top floor of each stage by climbing ladders, while avoiding enemies.

The stage layouts get more complex as the game progresses. There is a time limit in each stage, and the faster the top is reached, the better the score. Figuring out the best ways to reach the top gives the game a puzzle aspect, similar to titles such as Lode Runner.

However, in Ascend the player doesn't have the ability to dig holes. Instead, the player character can jump against blocks so that they can act as barriers for enemies, who would otherwise pose a danger as touching them leads to a loss of the limited lives of the player. There is also an exclamation mark symbol appearing during stages which gives invincibility once collected.

425268.overview: A scrolling screen platformer preview created by Søren Trautner Madsen & Klaus Schneyder and released as PD in 2022.

425355.overview: Embarrassing name aside, this is another vertically-scrolling, run-and-gun shooter, this time staring Terrapins, that may or may not bear a striking resemblance to other be-shelled pizza loving reptiles.

425362.overview: An action game where you've got to drive a smiley through a maze and reach the exit to the next stages. The game was created by Ron Coffen and released initiall on Loadstar #024 and #040 (version with new levels). It's got a maze-maker (level editor) in Loadstar #026.

425369.overview: A horizontal shooter made using the sideways SEUCK mod by Anthony Burns and released into the public domain in 2008.

425370.overview: A history game focused on the United States, created by Roger Norton and released on Loadstar #056 in 1989.

425438.overview: Move Ant Stiller's head around and collect 10 tophats while avoiding the falling dynamite and cake, which makes you fat and slow. Take the tophats to the target once you have them. Part of the 2022 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition from Cameron Davis.

425473.overview: Released in the 2020 C64 4kb Game Coding Competition (27th place), by Romwer. In the game you are the teleporter device. When a guy enters the teleporter, your job is to quickly guide him through the teleportation vortex, which humans can't see, of course. Wiggle your joystick to trace the path as fast as you can right after the teleportation process has started. You will see the vortex path briefly while the guy is walking towards the teleporter. It is your responsibility to memorize it thoroughly enough to not kill the person on his teleportation journey. Good luck!

425479.overview: A very strange C64 game from Italy, in which you control a flat rectangle (probably supposed to be a magic carpet), while trying to avoid strange enemies on the screen. The game's actual developer is unknown, but the game itself was published by Edisoft in Next No. 07 (11/1985).

425522.overview: Axel Butner II is a simple vertically scrolling shooter for 1-2 players (co-op) made by Frank Gasking using Chris Yates' Shoot Em Up Construction Kit. It was released in 1994, and was the prequel to his later game called Cybernator.

425528.overview: How does teleportation work? It's quite easy to explain. There is an invisible teleportation vortex, which carries the subject to its destination. In this game, YOU are the teleporter. Whenever a person enters, jour job is to recreate the vortex path using your joystick as quickly as possible.

425540.overview: A Hawkeye clone, scrolling screen platformer where you avoid the insects and grab the coins. You can jump, duck and play with a friend.

425655.overview:
Alienator! is a rail shooter that was created with SEUCK. It was re-released with some minor updates in 1993 and 2013.

Since sightings of dripping green slime. It turns out that now our base has been infested with hungy slimy green aliens. We need to destroy the base. A time bomb has been set to destroy all alien life forms on the site. 

You are Cassandra Richley and your mission is to escape from the base before the explosion. The only trouble is that she will be encountering various horrors. So arm yourself with an infinity laser rifle and start zapping.

425660.overview: One of the many games named "Aliens" for the platform, this one is a spanish first-person target shooter.

425668.overview: Another game named "Aliens", this one is a traditional space shooter.

425674.overview: Miner Wally (I see what they did there...) returns in this Christmas-themed revamp of the infamously difficult C64 single-screen platformer from 1984. But a bit of snow and a Santa costume isn't the only thing that's changed, Wally has now developed his athletic abilities beyond recognition to give you the player a fighting chance of actually completing a level and hopefully having a lot more fun along the way.....

444312.overview:
You are a lieutenant of the space explorers and you must explore a part of unknown space; you have an arrangement, a modular spaceship you can equip as you choose. All ship types have a minimum standard equipment: 1 radar and 10 points of fuel. As you discover planets and take exploratory missions, they will give you merit points and promotions. With every promotion you get a bigger and better equipped ship. The goal is to become Admiral in 10 missions or less.  
 
The three-dimensional space you will have to explore is divided into five sectors overlapping each other. Each sector is composed of 81 (9x9) quadrants of 1 parsec. Move from one quadrant to another of the same sector costs one fuel point; go up or down from one sector to another or make a hyperspace leap costs 5 fuel points. Be careful, the hyperspace leap is blind; even though remaining within the delimited space as above, the arrival point is regulated by the mysterious laws of galactic currents.

444315.overview: Initially, an Italian language selectable answer text adventure from Alessandro Castellari with RPG elements that was released in 1983. It would eventually be translated into English and have music added in 2023.

444339.overview:
The New Dimension in Co-op with Blazon are proud to present Alpacalypse. A fun run and jump, collect and avoid game, first  released on Zzap! 64 Micro Action #19's cover mount.

STORY

You are an Alpaca. You lived on a farm not far from the Mayan Temple. A sacred wonder in which druids had worshiped many events – that's what you probably think. Unfortunately, some silly nutcase had left your pen open, and you escaped. It was peaceful outside the Mayan Temple, not a human in sight. You run into the temple. Just as you reach the central point of it, you hear a click and then the ground shakes. Suddenly, you feel as if the temple is growing. Not quite, because you are being sent to the underground towards a blazing inferno. Now your Alpaca is running for its life in a bid for freedom. Behold the Alpacalypse.

PLAYING THE GAME

This game is for one player only. Alpacalypse is a horizontal scrolling run and jump game, which features eight levels. Your task is to guide your Alpaca safely across each level of the underground lair inside the Mayan Temple. The temple underground is under a spell, which wraps around the scenery. It is up to you to help your Alpaca to travel all the way to freedom.

COMPLETING A LEVEL

In order to complete a level, your Alpaca must travel a complete distance that has been set in the top left of the score panel. (XX/YY) Where XX is the distance you have currently travelled and YY is the target distance before completing a level.

BONUS POINTS

On completing a level, you will score bonus points, according to the amount of energy that is left. Units of 100 points per bonus will be added to the score.

OBSTACLES

During game play. Your Alpaca will not be alone. In fact, you will be facing a series of various in game obstacles that should be avoided or can be useful. They are as follows:

THE FIREBALLS AND ENEMIES


Your Alpaca will not be alone. The temple underground also consists of eight different evil spirits, rumored to be controlled by aliens. These baddies will try and drain as much energy from you every time they hit you. The aliens range from spiritual figures to alien spacecraft. The type of behavior varies on the type of aliens that appear inside the scenery.



These range from alien ships, to spiders, fish, and Mayan artifacts. Also, from all four directions, groups of fireballs could appear. Colliding into aliens and fireballs will drain your energy, but they will be killed instantly. As soon as your Alpaca’s energy is out – you will lose a life.

448416.overview: Arwag is an unreleased role-playing game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Megastyle. The playable demo version was released in 2012.

450031.overview: Ace Harrier is an unreleased pseudo-3D shooter in the same vein as Space Harrier. The game was developed by Robert Flynn. The playable demo was released in 1986, but not much is known about the game other than that,

450498.overview:
Alien Strike (also known as The Unexpected) is a 1-player space shooter for the Commodore 64.

It was developed by Behzad Jamshidi and published as a type-in listing in RUN 1990/04.

451333.overview: A 1989 compilation cartridge featuring one Parker Brothers game and three Activision games: Frogger, River Raid, Decathlon and Beamrider. It was released by HES Australia.

451427.overview: A compilation of Archon Games including the original Archon: The Light and the Dark, the updated and more complex Archon II: Adept and the homebrew Archon III - Exciter along with some bonus music all loading in turbo fast speed in cartridge form.

453345.overview: The first ever game that is controlled by the Commodore 1530 Datassette hardware device. However there is a trainer mode that allows you to use the spacebar instead of just the datassette play button. First available at the 2024 Zoo Party. An undersea Skramble-style, horizontally scrolling shooter where you blast the creatures and pick up the sunken treasures.

454047.overview: This is an updated version of the top scrolling and somewhat difficult shoot'em up game, Abyssal Karma. Many things have been fixed in this update. It also includes new enemies, a final boss, and an ending screen. It was created by Rodrigo Yeowtch and the latest version came out in 2025. A classic shoot 'em up game created in the SEUCK editor. During the flight, you must collect P letters, which increase the range of your weapon. There are 3 long stages to complete and a battle with the final boss.

454538.overview:
Adventures on Planet Smir is a science fiction themed text adventure for the Commodore 64.

It was developed by Joseph "HarryPotter" Rose, and released into the public domain in 2024.

454887.overview:
Apple Fall is a single-screen platform game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Gary Turner and Andrew Wilson, and published in the following:

- Commodore Horizons 1983/12-1984/01
- PIXEL #02 (05-06/1984)

455607.overview: "Asterix en Obelix" is a Connect Four-style game developed for the Commodore 64. In this two-player game, each player is represented by one of the iconic characters: Asterix or Obelix. The objective is to strategically place pieces on the board to connect four in a row before the opponent does. The game was programmed and graphically designed by Dieter Jansky and is presented in German. It utilizes keyboard controls and supports both PAL and NTSC systems. The game is relatively compact, occupying 37 blocks of memory.

455640.overview: A single player, graphics and text adventure created by Norbert Klein and published in both 64'er Sonderheft 1986/04, and 64'er Sonderheft 60.

455641.overview:
This is a C64 BASIC conversion of Soleau Software's shareware MS-DOS game, originally developed by William Soleau in 1992. In this game you control Alpha Man on a 11x7 grid where the object is to push blue blocks with letters on them over tiles marked with the same letter. Sounds like a very simple task, but the actual solution of each puzzle in this game can prove to be very challenging. (Part of the reason why I chose to make this conversion.)

There are a few notable differences between the original game and this version:

1. Just like the DOS version, this one also has a save feature, though significantly simplified to merely saving all the records into a single file, instead of creating and managing "player cards". If you intend to use the load/save feature, make it sure that you have a writeable floppy disk in drive 8, either physically or virtually.

2. In this version of the game, the tiles and the possible letter markings on them are obscured by the blocks and the player standing over them. This can be taken as added difficulty, but to avoid unnecessary confusion, when a letter block is positioned over a matching tile, it becomes purple.

3. The original game provides an option to demonstrate a solution for the first few puzzles. This one doesn't, but I don't believe not having this feature is a huge loss.

This game offers the same 25 word puzzles as the shareware version of Soleau's Alpha Man. The full version adds another 25 puzzles, which I'd be glad to add to the next C64 Alpha Man later, but until then, I wish you to have a lot of fun with this one.

455770.overview:
The ancient holy island of Avalan, once home to the mysterious sky wizards, the creators of excalibruh, the great master sword.

An unholy Monk has swept onto the island, stealing all its holy relics and has shattered the master sword into pieces. The Monk has also enlisted a huge army of skilled soldiers ready to battle all who try to oppose him.

Find the pieces to the great sword Excalibruh and send the Monk packing back to his stinky old bedsit.

456053.overview: Astroclash is a somewhat simplistic 1-player fixed shooter for the Commodore 64. The game was developed and released by Noltisoft in 2017.

456267.overview: A short little entry for the Mini Jame Gam #40: Ad Popper, made in 48 hours. The player sits in front of an infected computer, whose monitor displays annoying pop-up windows. Each window that remains open increases the computer's usage, so they must be closed quickly. From time to time, a window appears offering the installation of turrets that provide three missiles for use. The game ends when the computer's processor becomes overloaded.

456378.overview: A scrolling sci-fi themed shooter developed by Mr. GJ and Bon using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and released into the publc domain in 2010.

456450.overview:
Written by Sander Alsema for the 10-liner competition 2025.

--- Description & Instructions ---

While wandering through the savannah, Kevin suddenly feels an appetite
building up. If he were a human being, then he would have had a serious
problem. Kevin, however, is not a human being but an aardvark. For him
the absence of a McDonald's franchise doesn't mean certain death from
starvation. Normally he would simply hurl out his tongue towards the
first ant or termite crossing his path, but not today. Under the
influence of narcotics Kevin's head has become detached from his body,
making it too hard to catch anything all by himself. This is where you
come in...

Press 'A' to let Kevin Aardvark know when to stick out his tongue.
Every time you catch an ant, Kevin's head floats to the right. Because
this is where the ants are coming from, your job becomes increasingly
harder. Every ant you miss will cost you a life, and you only have three
of those. After that, it's game over. But should you manage to catch 30
ants, then Kevin has had enough, and you will win the game!

Afterwards, press any key to play again.

456482.overview: An adventure game created using 3D Constructor Kit. The player takes on the role of a pastor whose task is to defeat a demon holding the villagers captive. The player moves around locations looking for items necessary to complete the game. To do this, use the crosshairs and the fire button to pick up an item or perform an action with an active object. Where the flag is located, there is a descent from the cliff, and you can only enter the water with diving equipment. There are many such solutions in the game, which requires the player to be observant and experiment.

456643.overview: Blueberries is a single player run and gun shooter developed by Alf Yngve using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit, and released in 1992.

456734.overview:
The Ark of Exodus is a text adventure for the C64. It was developed by Grant Thomson, who also developed a follow-up game called The Starchild.

The year of release is not known.

456889.overview:
Football is played over four 25-minute quarters. When you get control of the ball, you can either kick or punch (“handball”) it. The game is designed to simulate the real game so that kicks will normally travel farther than hand¬ balls.

The program assumes you are shooting for goal if you are within scoring distance, and you kick the ball the required distance. If you are, for example, 30 meters from goal, and you kick the ball 35 meters, the program will assume that you've shot on goal.

There are four “goal posts” at each end of the playing oval. The center two posts are taller than the outside pair. If the ball goes between the two center posts, a goal is scored. If the ball hits one of the posts, or goes between a tall post and a shorter one, only a point is scored. At the end of the game, the number of goals is multiplied by six, the single points added, to get the total number of the strangely named “behinds.” The winning team—naturally enough—is the one which scores the most behinds. 
 
Published in the book "Second Giant Book of Computer Games".

456955.overview:
Arabian Treasurehunt is a German single-screen platform game for the Commodore 64.

It was developed by Champ-Soft and published in the following:

-  Happy Computer 1985/12
-  64'er Spielesammlung #3

456975.overview: The player's task is to get three birds to the flower at the same time. The game is controlled by pressing the fire button, which increases the flight ceiling of the birds, which are constantly falling down due to gravity. The faster you press, the faster they fly. Colliding with any obstacle means you have to start the journey from the beginning.

457096.overview: The player's task is to defeat Zeglar in an uneven pistol duel. Zeglar has more energy and the player must move forward and backwards accordingly to prevent the opponent's bullets from reaching their target. Each successive bullet can be fired when the previous one disappears from the screen, so shortening the distance to the opponent speeds them up.

457141.overview: The Wonders of The Animal Kingdom is an educational game for ages six to twelve that consists of six learning activities. The game intends to train a number of skills including reading comprehension, science knowledge, spelling, memory, logic and pattern recognition.

457167.overview: A game of taking over your opponent's pawns. There are full and hole pawns to choose from on an 8x8 board. The movement consists of jumping one or more pawns from their position to the first empty field behind the opponent's pawn vertically, horizontally and diagonally. Jumped pawns change their appearance to that of the pawn that jumped them. The game ends when all the squares are occupied and the player with the most captured pawns is the winner.

457371.overview: As commander of the space ship, your objective is to navigate the asteroid belt without being struck. Fuel depletes over time, so you will need to continually intercept fuel pods (yellow dots) before it runs out. There are also UFOs in the area, so be careful!

457432.overview:
Asterofield II is a simple side scrolling shooter for the C64. It was developed and released by Noltisoft in 2022.

Despite the name, there was no Asterofield 1.

457492.overview:
One of two games of the same name published by Tronic Verlag in an issue of their magazine Compute mit.

This one is an underwater themed game developed by Einsteinsoftware. During your last summer vacation at the seaside, you stumbled upon the remains of the legendary underwater city of Atlantis while diving. As you know from the city's history, treasures of immeasurable proportions are hidden there. You now want to recover these ancient treasures of the Atlanteans. But unfortunately, someone else has gotten wind of the treasure and your discovery: You have no choice but to dive for the treasures in winter. Since the water is, of course, freezing cold, you can't stay underwater for more than two minutes; otherwise, you'll freeze to death and lose one of your three lives. Furthermore, you must be careful not to run out of oxygen, hit a rock, or come into contact with the monsters.

It was published in Compute mit 1985/09.

457522.overview:
The Astronauts is a 1-player public domain miscellaneous space themed game for the Commodore 64.

It was developed and released by Antsoft in 1984.

457847.overview:
Ace is a 2 player only Tron Light Cycles game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Matthias Kramm.

While the game is a full game, for whatever reason, the game was not officially released.

457882.overview:
Artemis is an 1-player archery shooting game for the Commodore 64..

The game was developed by D. Dziwosz and released in Input 64 1985/04.

457964.overview:
Air Wolf (not to be confused with Airwolf) is a two player only versus duel helicopter shooter for the Commodore 64.

It's different than other duel shooters, as there is also computer controlled helicopters that get in the way as well.

The game was developed by Antsoft and released for free in 1985.

459495.overview: Aqualique X is a modernized spiritual successor to the minimalist real-time strategy game Aqualique 10, originally written by Commocore in just 10 lines of BASIC for the Commodore 64. Staying faithful to the core mechanics and the tone of the original, Aqualique X try to expand on the concept with deeper gameplay, improved visuals, and enhanced strategic depth.

459573.overview: You play the role of Sam Boon, an L.A. Private Detective, or you will be. You recently received your permit to practice and have just moved into a new office. Hopefully, you will get a case soon as the first month's rent is due in a few days and you can't currently afford it. If you don't get a case your career will end before it has begun.

459823.overview:
Control your ants to find food. Beware of spicy spots and spiders. Play with joystick in port 2, or use WASD. Press fire or space to start.

Developed and released by Demesos as part of the 536th One Hour Game Jam.

460451.overview: The player's task is to guide a cute bee to a flower. The game is controlled by pressing the shoot button, which increases the bee's flight altitude as it continuously falls down due to gravity. The faster you press, the faster the bee flies. Colliding with any obstacle, including a cloud, means you have to start the journey from the beginning.

460609.overview: The player takes on the role of an astronaut with a backpack and a laser who, in some unknown way, finds himself in a medieval world full of bizarre creatures. During the journey, various items must be collected and used appropriately. Some are used immediately, while others only after selecting the appropriate command. The laser can be used to exterminate enemies, although some of them are immune to the player's weapon. In general, you must find all the parts of two axes and take them to the ruler of this strange world. It is also important to remember that the player can only carry two items at a time. Those that have been used must be discarded from the inventory. Collisions with hostile creatures drain energy, which can be replenished by using collected food and drinks. Some creatures and traps are permanently deadly to our hero.

460640.overview: The player takes on the role of a woman who does not know where she is. The player's task is to choose options that will lead the woman safely home. Wrong decisions usually result in various types of death.

460731.overview: The player takes on the role of a spy whose task is to reach the alien ship, blow it up and escape. Otherwise, Earth will be destroyed by a powerful bomb. The game is divided into six stages. In the first stage, you must avoid being trapped in falling cages. The second stage involves skilfully dodging lasers while flying on an air scooter. In the third stage, you must reach the starting point with a robot under bomb fire. The fourth requires precision in avoiding asteroids. In the fifth, you must reach the ammunition room to pick up a rifle to fight alien robots, and in the last one, you must board the appropriate ship and escape from the station before it explodes.

460762.overview: A strategic game for two players. Players place pieces of their colour on the board and try to surround their opponent's pieces. If this manoeuvre is successful, all surrounded pieces are moved to the captured pieces pool. The player who has more of their opponent's captured pieces and creates more single ‘eyes’ on the board wins. If it is impossible to make a move or if the next move may reduce the number of points, the player must place their piece in the PASS field.

460781.overview:
The idea of the game is to complete your bank of cards, Ace to 10, before the computer. With the exception of playing wild card Jacks, this game is mostly based on the luck of the card shuffle.

Released as part of a BASIC only card game development competition.

460791.overview: A SEUCK game developed by Roberto Riccioppo of TND and released in 2016.

460819.overview:
Alien Attack I is the first of a series of Commercial SEUCK games developed and released by Champion Software (Wil Smith & Ron Burghes).

The game draws inspiration from the popular Alien franchise.

The game is a 1-2 player co-op game.

460820.overview:
The second game in Champion Software's Alien Attack series.

The game is a 1-2 player co-op game.

460830.overview:
The third and final game in the Alien Attack Series from Champion Software.

Like the previous two games, this is a 1-2 player co-op game.

460839.overview: A slightly unusual variation on classic Tetris. The player arranges falling blocks of various shapes, trying to keep the height of the fill as low as possible until a certain time has elapsed. Arranging a full row causes it to disappear, which lowers the height. When the time is up, the number of unfilled levels on the board is counted and the game calculates the points earned by the player based on this. Additional points are earned by clearing rows and accelerating the downward direction of the blocks. At each level, the player receives a parachute, which allows them to briefly stop the block in place by using the upward direction. The game ends if any block touches the top edge of the board.

460851.overview: Alps is a simple platformer created by Brian Bagnall using Garry Kitchen's GameMaker.

460855.overview: A single-player only SEUCK game developed and released by Indy Software as part of SEUCK Compo 2013.

460862.overview:
This is a traditional game with a difference. You play it against the computer. The computer knows the rules of the game, but it does not know how to win. At first it makes its moves entirely at random, so you stand a good chance of winning. But, after you have played against it several times, it makes good moves more often and bad moves less often. It learns from its mistakes and takes note of its successes. You may then find it much more difficult to beat it.
This simple game is a fascinating one in its own right. Played against a computer which is capable of learning to improve its play is a somewhat unusual experience. 

Published in the book "The Commodore 64 Games Book - 21 Sensational Games".

460863.overview:
"Aquantor" was named Happy Computer "Game of the Month. Christian Stredicke's game is original and unusual from the very beginning: a labyrinth being flooded by water. If the player isn't careful, everything will soon be saturated with the blue liquid. 
 
Published in both Happy Computer 1985/10,  and in 64'er Spielesammlung #2.

460875.overview: Published as Libra in 64'er Sonderheft 1985/03, 64'er Spielesammlung #2 and as Atom in Compute mit 1986/12.

460879.overview: The player's task is to paint over all the paths of the grid while avoiding spinning objects. The paint is taken from the purple area, and the player must paint over the grid cells to fill them, thereby increasing the range of the source. Moving too far away from the paint source or moving backwards in the opposite direction will interrupt the painting process. There is only one life in the game, and losing it means starting all over again.

460900.overview: The player's task is to find all pairs of randomly scattered cards with different stones within a specified time. Finding the right pair removes the cards from the board, while the wrong ones are covered again, giving the player the opportunity to remember their location. The game exercises visual memory.

461173.overview: Alpha Aliens is a simple sci-fi themed crosshairs shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Neil Philips and published in Commodore User 1985/05

462268.overview:
The Alpha Test is a single-player educational math game for the Commodore 64.

It was developed by Barbara H. Schulak and Maurice jones, and published in Loadstar #073 in 1990.

462387.overview: A public domain German language Breakout clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed  and released by BB Software (Roland Kunz). The year of release is not known.

462688.overview: A strategy game for two players in which you must move all your pieces to the other side. The game is similar to Backgammon, but has slightly different rules. In each turn, the player rolls two dice and can move one or two pieces, always forward. If the player rolls two identical numbers, e.g. 5 and 5, they receive a double move and can move any 4 pieces 5 spaces. If they roll 2 and 1, the player makes a normal move and chooses any two double numbers, gaining 4 moves and an additional turn to play. An opponent's piece can be captured if it is alone on a rectangular square. If there is more than one opponent's piece on the square, it is not possible to move to that square. A captured piece is always placed first after the turn begins.

462703.overview: The player starts the game with a pot of £100, and at the beginning two cards are drawn, e.g. 3 and 9. Then the player bets any amount, and if the next card is between 3 and 9, they win; if not, they lose.

462704.overview: The player starts the game with a pot of $1,500, and two cards are drawn at the beginning, e.g. 3 and 9. The player then bets any amount, and if the next card is between 3 and 9, they win; if not, they lose.

462910.overview: Acid is a public domain 2-plyaer only versus duel shooter for the Commodore 64. it was developed by and released by SaNiTy in 2000.

463300.overview: A demo of an unreleased homebrew port of Another World/Out of This World for the c64

464128.overview: An educational maths game for young children, in which the friendly Alf teaches addition and subtraction.

465116.overview: A rally across Africa with unpredictable and random events. At the beginning, the player has $300 and chooses one of five cars equipped with basic supplies. Driving involves pressing any key and the left or right arrow keys. Each keystroke generates a one-day event to which the player must respond appropriately. Each day, the player travels 50 miles, and at the end of the day, statistics on fuel, oil and water consumption and the condition of the vehicle are displayed. Some events require very quick reflexes, such as an armed attack by natives. All supplies can be replenished and repairs made after reaching cities along the route. The game ends when, for example, water or fuel runs out, or when the player's vehicle is destroyed in an accident.

465717.overview: Using a combat ship, the player's task is to shoot down 10 objects shaped like the logos of well-known computer brands in each stage. Each object shot down leaves behind a coin, which must be collected before it disappears. The coins can be used to purchase upgrades and additional energy, which is lost when the ship collides with any moving objects. The game ends when the player's ship is destroyed.

466605.overview: Collect all the flags scattered around the platforms to advance to the next level. Ghosts try to stop you and must be avoided. Platforms can be scrolled left and right to line up ladders for access to the different levels.

466718.overview: Alesian Plains is a fantasy themed text adventure for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Paul Allen Panks and released in 2004.

466720.overview:
Agricola is a public domain German language trading simulation with a farming theme for 1-4 players.

The game was developed by M.U.S. Software and published in the following:

-   Digital Marketing PD #094
-   Stonysoft #0089
-   Stonysoft #0519

466738.overview: Avoid is a single-player avoid it game for the Commodore 64. It was developed and released by Kay Tichelmann in 1992.

467504.overview: A classic pinball game in which you use flippers to bounce a ball around, trying to hit scoring areas.

468193.overview: Devlab/TSA is proud to present our Commodore 64 game Amirun and the alien beerscuckers. Our take on a "Pooyan" clone, more specifically inspired by "Pigs from Space" (1984), which was itself a clone of Pooyan.

469667.overview: Asteroides is a Spanish language avoid it game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Angel Garcia Delgado and published in 1985 as part of Commodore Computer Club N°07

471152.overview:
The game was created using the TRSE development tool based on Bery's (Zsolt Bertók) work of the same name for Videoton TV Computer.

Axis is an "escape" game where our protagonist cannot hit or shoot, only run. The story can be read at the beginning of the game. The point is: we have to escape from aliens and get out through the exit door (two red arrows pointing down). To do this, we need to pick up key cards (red and green) to open the doors of the corresponding color. The aliens are faster than the protagonist, and if they sense/see us (even through walls!) they will immediately rush towards us (attack). So caution, patience, and skill will be needed to avoid them.

The game measures the time spent on the track (so it doesn't go between tracks, you can safely leave the machine between two tracks).

There are 10 sectors, at the end of the 10th the protagonist gets out, and we can admire the end sequence and take pictures of the time that has passed :)

During the game, you can switch to faster speed by pressing the '+' key, but the aliens will also be faster. You can switch back to the original speed by pressing the '-' key.

The M key can be used to turn the music on/off.

The game is controlled with the WASD keys and the joystick plugged into port 2. The door is opened with the 'SPACE' key, or the fire button on the joy.

471855.overview:
Alliance is a 2 player only German language board game for the Commodore 64.

It was developed by Rainer Kaufmann and published in Telematch 1984/05-06.

472096.overview: Both keyboard or joystick can be used to play. Keyboard controls: WASD to move, SPACE for action.

472139.overview: Addix is a classic 2 player game, you play against the computer. You select a number from the current row, using SPACE then ENTER to move.

472147.overview: The player takes on the role of a UFO pilot whose task is to rescue five castaways. To do this, they use a tractor beam with a limited range, so they must fly very low to the ground to pick up an alien. Pulling a cow on board, or colliding with dangerous objects and their missiles, automatically destroys the player’s saucer, forcing them to restart the mission. Fortunately, the UFO is equipped with missiles that can be used to destroy enemy objects and cows.

473128.overview: You have an art block (however you may interpret that), so you wander the city, suburbs, and nature looking for scenes to draw into your sketchbook. After you have gathered 10 drawings, go to the museum and submit your sketchbook.

474136.overview: Super Alien is a single-screen action game. The player moves through the maze and can place traps on the floor. When a monster walks into it, it becomes trapped and the player can kill it by filling in the hole. Each defeated monster rewards points while touching them results in a life loss. The maze is shown from the usual top-down perspective, but the characters have a side-view.

475411.overview: This time, Adrian's adventure takes place across six new, larger, and more diverse worlds featuring an even greater number of enemies. Adrian's mission remains the same: to help Crystian find one lost almost-crystal in each world.

478243.overview: You control your reconnaissance vehicle across the unpredictable surface of Alien Planet. But the calm is deceptive: the horizon never seems to get any closer, while an army of alien creatures descends upon you! Quick reflexes are essential if you want to fight your way through the waves of alien attackers.

478529.overview: ALPHA JONG is a fully authentic Alphanumeric Mahjong simulator developed natively in 100% Assembly for the legendary Commodore 64. Enjoy the classic Riichi mechanics without the language barrier as you compete against the AI in a desperate race to complete your 14-tile hand

478545.overview: All About Colours is an educational software title from Grolier / Mindflight that was recently recovered from long-term archival loss in August 2026

480087.overview: A physics simulation of a rocket launch. Can you get your rocket into orbit? Select your rocket configuration first, the start the engine with w and steer rocket with wasd.

480366.overview: A Day at the Races is a classic‑style horse‑racing simulation with simple controls and fast gameplay. Study the runners, place your bets, and work your way through the racing calendar to earn a place in the Main Event.

480455.overview: A reworking of Taito's Arkanoid to fix issues with NTSC, especially at higher levels and to enable better CBM mouse support.

481073.overview:
Stacker (or Stacker Club) machines have become a classic in modern arcades and entertainment centers. Designed by LAI Games , these skill-based machines combine incredibly simple mechanics with high visual tension. 

This time, from the keyboards of Minter , we bring you a version for our system.
The objective of the game is very intuitive.

Mechanics: LED light blocks move horizontally back and forth on a vertical screen. The player must press the button at the exact moment to stack the blocks on top of each other.

Progression: As the tower climbs to the top, the support surface decreases and the speed of movement increases, demanding maximum precision and reflexes.

481356.overview:
Not to be confused with Arcade Classics from Firebird Software (which was four clones of classic early arcade games like Asteroids and Space Invaders).

Arcade Classics published by U.S. Gold  is a compilation containing the following four previously released OFFICIAL arcade conversions all of which originally published by Atarisoft as well as Datasoft:

-    Pole Position
-    Dig-Dug
-    Mr. Do!
-    Pac-Man

481631.overview: A real-time action roguelite for the Commodore 64. Descend 60 floors of an old mine, keep the eight soul lamps of Dunmere burning, and silence the Ashheart.

481722.overview: Fight a hopeless battle against an attacking alien race. There is no hope of victory, only to take as many enemies down with you, as you can!

481741.overview: The player takes on the role of a submarine operator and must navigate through six stages of varying lengths, whilst avoiding being hit by missiles and colliding with enemy creatures. For defence, the player has torpedoes, with a firing rate limited to one missile visible on the screen at any one time. For every 10,000 points, the player receives an additional submarine. Once all stages have been completed, the game loops and you start all over again.

481836.overview:
The ultimate 16-bit football game comes to the Commodore 64/128!

For the last five years I have been thinking of attempting to port Sensible Soccer to the C64 and had the pitch and sprites ready to go, but unlike my arcade ports I knew just 'eyeballing' the gameplay would not be enough, with the feel of the game down to the precise way players and the ball move, and how they interact with each other. You could easily make a game that looks like Sensi (I'm looking at you, Graeme Souness International Soccer....), but making it play like it would require intimate knowledge of the game's workings.

481984.overview:
Atari's two arcade machines, Asteroids (1979) and Asteroids Deluxe (1980), on a Commodore 64. These are not remakes: the arcade machine's own program runs on the C64's processor, and the machine around it is emulated: the vector display, the clock and interrupt, the switches, the sound board and, for Deluxe, the POKEY.

This package is the source of that emulator, and everything needed to build it. It holds nothing of the arcade programs. To get the games you build them from the arcade ROMs, which you supply.

481986.overview:
Atari's two arcade machines, Asteroids (1979) and Asteroids Deluxe (1980), on a Commodore 64. These are not remakes: the arcade machine's own program runs on the C64's processor, and the machine around it is emulated: the vector display, the clock and interrupt, the switches, the sound board and, for Deluxe, the POKEY.

This package is the source of that emulator, and everything needed to build it. It holds nothing of the arcade programs. To get the games you build them from the arcade ROMs, which you supply.

482263.overview: A complete unedited match between a human player and an AI opponent in Awesome Slam Sibs Infinite. - and Yes, I have changed the game title slightly to make it even more insane

482560.overview: A little pumpkin has been invited to tea – by a friendly family of aliens waiting at Area 51. The way there is long, the castle walls are high, and pumpkins can't jump. Luckily the spider next door has plenty of silk to spare…

482761.overview: Astral Jack is a single-screen arcade platformer in the spirit of the 1980s classics, written in 6502 assembly for the Commodore 64: chunky dithered pixels, purple and blue bricks, olive grass, and a bright crescent moon on pure black.

482795.overview: Trapped in a haunted villa. Find the 8 magic numbers in the right order, avoid the ghost and the rotten basement floor, and escape before the villa keeps you forever! ABANDONED VILLA 2 is a spooky picture adventure for the Commodore 64, written in 100% 6502 machine code. You are trapped in an abandoned villa where eight magic numbers are hidden. Explore nine rooms, each with its own picture: flickering candles, glowing eyes, bats, spiders and lightning at the windows. A ghost wanders the halls and the basement floor is rotten. Find the numbers 1 to 8 in the right order and escape through the front door. There are 3 lives, the numbers are hidden in different rooms every game, and SID music and sound effects play throughout.
